漫画	màn huà	comics; cartoon; manga — 漫 màn (free; unrestrained) + 画 huà (drawing). A free, sketchy drawing: the word for comics and cartoons. The same two characters name Japanese manga, where they are read manga.
盲目	máng mù	blindly; without judgment; reckless — 盲 (blind) + 目 (eye). An intensified compound where both characters carry the same meaning: acting as though blind, without seeing the situation clearly. 盲目乐观 mángmù lèguān means "blindly optimistic"; 盲目跟风 means to follow trends without thinking.
毛笔	máo bǐ	writing brush; ink brush — 毛 máo (hair; fur) + 笔 bǐ. The classic soft-tipped brush of calligraphy and ink painting, named for the animal hair of its tuft. The tool that gives Chinese writing its living, varying line.
毛病	máo bìng	defect, flaw, bad habit; malfunction — 毛 (máo) means fine hair or fur, here the trivial detail; 毛病 is a small fault that keeps recurring. It stretches across a machine that breaks down, a person's annoying habit, and a minor recurring ailment, all the everyday senses of "something is wrong with it."
毛茶	máo chá	rough tea / mao cha — the uncompressed base material
毛泽东	Máo Zé dōng	Mao Zedong — predecessor, contrast
矛盾论	máo dùn lùn	On Contradiction — On Contradiction: Mao Zedong's 1937 philosophical essay applying materialist dialectics to political analysis. One of the two foundational texts of Mao Zedong Thought (alongside 实践论 Shíjiàn Lùn, "On Practice").
茅屋	máo wū	thatched hut; humble dwelling — 茅 máo (thatch grass) + 屋 wū (dwelling). A simple hut roofed with grass. The 茅屋 is a literary image of humble, virtuous poverty , the dwelling of the reclusive scholar or hermit.
冒出	mào chū	to pop up; to suddenly emerge
贸易公司	mào yì gōng sī	trading company
没吃	méi chī	didn't eat; have not eaten — 没(有) is the standard negator for completed actions. It replaces 了 entirely , you never say 没吃了, because 没 already carries the information that no completion occurred. The 了 is superfluous and wrong. This is a near-universal rule: 没 and post-verb 了 are mutually exclusive.
没错	méi cuò	that's right; exactly; no mistake — 没 méi (not have) + 错 cuò (error). "No error here," used to agree firmly: 没错，我就是这个意思 "exactly, that's just what I mean." Often softened to 没错儿 in northern speech.
没道理	méi dào lǐ	unreasonable; makes no sense; unjust — 没 méi (lack; without) + 道理 dàolǐ (reason; logic). "Without reason": lacking the logic or justice to be acceptable. Used when something is not just inconvenient but genuinely wrong in its reasoning or fairness.
没关系	méi guān xi	it doesn't matter; never mind; that's okay — One of the most indispensable phrases in Mandarin. The standard response to 对不起 (sorry). Literally "no relationship" , meaning "it has no effect on us; it carries no weight." Learn this before your first week of speaking Chinese.
没礼貌	méi lǐ mào	rude; ill-mannered; lacking in manners — 没 méi (lacks; does not have) + 礼貌. The standard rebuke. Heavier than English "rude" because it implies a failure of formation, not just a momentary lapse.
没面子	méi miàn zi	to lose face; to be embarrassed; without prestige — To be without face , whether because one has lost it through embarrassing behavior or because one's status is insufficient to command it. 没面子 is the social embarrassment register, distinct from the moral shame of 丢脸.
没事	méi shì	it's nothing; no problem; never mind; to be free (not busy) — 没 méi (not have) + 事 shì. "No matter." The everyday reassurance: it's fine, don't worry, no harm done. Also literally "to have nothing on," to be free.
没问题	méi wèn tí	no problem; sure; that's fine — One of the most useful everyday phrases, used to agree to a request, reassure, or confirm that something will be fine. Equivalent to "no problem / sure / consider it done." A warm, willing reply.
没意思	méi yì si	boring; pointless; not interesting — The negation of 有意思 , lacking appeal, engagement, or point. Can describe activities, conversations, people, or situations. Often used for mild complaint rather than outright criticism. 说没意思的话 (to say pointless things) is a common mild rebuke.
梅雨	méi yǔ	plum rains
每天 · 天天	měi tiān tiān tiān	every day · day after day (emphatic) — 每天 měitiān: 每 měi (every; each) + 天 tiān (day). The neutral distributive "every day." 每 attaches to any time unit: 每年 (every year), 每月 (every month), 每周 (every week).
美德	měi dé	a virtue; an admirable quality — 美 měi (beautiful; admirable) + 德. A beautiful virtue , a particular admirable quality, usable as a count noun. 谦虚是一种美德 "humility is a virtue." 中华民族的传统美德 "the traditional virtues of the Chinese nation" is one of the standard formulas in civic discourse.
美感	měi gǎn	aesthetic sense; sense of beauty — 美 měi + 感 gǎn (feeling; sense). The capacity to perceive and appreciate beauty. Used in art criticism, design, and discussions of taste. 有美感 "has a good aesthetic sense" · 缺乏美感 "lacks aesthetic awareness."
美国	Měi guó	USA (lit. "beautiful country") — 美 měi (beautiful) + 国 guó. From the phonetic transcription of "America" (亚美利加 Yà-Měi-lì-jiā), with 美 selected as both sound-match and flattering character. A lucky phonetic fit.
美好	měi hǎo	beautiful; wonderful
美化	měi huà	to beautify; to prettify; to whitewash — 美 měi (beautiful) + 化 huà (the -ize suffix). Literally "to make beautiful." 美化 covers both the literal beautifying of a place (planting flowers, cleaning streets) and the figurative dressing-up of something unattractive, that is, putting a flattering gloss on a person, a record, or a history.
美丽	měi lì	beautiful (poetic, elevated) — 美 měi + 丽 lì (splendid; brilliant , originally: a deer with fine antlers). Used for landscapes, natural scenes, and elevated emotional beauty. More literary than 漂亮. 美丽的风景 "beautiful scenery" · 美丽的心灵 "a beautiful soul."
美女	měi nǚ	miss (lit. beauty); address for a young woman
美食	měi shí	delicious food; gourmet cuisine; gastronomy — 美 měi (beautiful; excellent) + 食 shí (food; to eat). Fine food; delicacies. Used everywhere food culture is celebrated , travel blogs, TV shows, restaurant descriptions. 美食家 měishíjiā = gourmet; food connoisseur.
昧良心	mèi liáng xīn	to go against one's conscience; to act in bad faith — 昧 mèi (to obscure; to violate knowingly). 昧良心 is the standard phrase for suppressing what one's conscience perceives and doing wrong anyway , the act Wang Yangming calls covering the sun with clouds.
门槛	mén kǎn	threshold (canonical object of 跨过)
门口	mén kǒu	doorway; entrance — 门 mén (door) + 口 kǒu (mouth; opening). The mouth of the door, the spot just at the entrance: 在门口等 "to wait at the door," 学校门口 "the school gate."
门派	mén pài	martial sect; faction
门票	mén piào	entrance ticket: an admission ticket; the entry fee — 门 mén (door; gate; entrance) + 票 piào (slip; ticket). The ticket that admits you through the gate: into a park, a museum, a temple, a concert. By extension it also names the price of admission, what you pay at the door.
门神	mén shen	door god; guardian deity of the threshold
闷黄	mèn yuáng	smothering / yellowing — the defining yellow tea step
蒙古人	Měng gǔ rén	Mongols — first class — Rulers and military commanders. Held supreme authority. Exempt from many taxes. Administered the empire primarily in Mongolian. Kublai maintained a deliberately Mongolian court culture even as he adopted many Chinese administrative forms.
孟姜女	Mèng Jiāng nǚ	Meng Jiangnu (the wall-weeping legend)
孟子	Mèng zǐ	Mencius — the second great Confucian philosopher — Mengzi (372–289 BCE) developed Confucian thought in two crucial directions: the argument for the innate goodness of human nature (性善论 xìngshàn lùn , humans are naturally oriented toward virtue), and a robust theory of political legitimacy based on the welfare of the people.
梦见	mèng jiàn	to see in a dream, to dream of
梦想	mèng xiǎng	dream; aspiration; to dream of — 梦 mèng (dream; to dream) + 想 xiǎng (thought; aspiration). Dream-thought: a vision held in the heart that exceeds the present reality. Warmer and more personal than 理想 (which has a principled, philosophical register); closer to the English "dream" in the sense of a cherished personal ambition.
迷路	mí lù	to lose one's way, to get lost — 迷 mí (confused, lost) + 路 lù (road). Literally "to be confused about the road." Used for getting lost in a city, in mountains, or on the way to somewhere. The figurative sense (losing one's moral or career direction) usually prefers 迷失方向 míshī fāngxiàng or 走错路 zǒu cuò lù.
迷失方向	mí shī fāng xiàng	to lose one's bearings; to be lost (literally or figuratively) — 迷 (mí, to be confused; to lose oneself) + 失 (shī, to lose) + 方向. A heavier and more poetic version of 失去方向. Used for someone literally lost in a forest or city, but more often for someone in a moral, professional, or personal crisis. Common in advice writing, sermons, and the chorus of pop songs.
迷信	mì xìn	superstition
密封	mì fēng	to seal hermetically; airtight — 密 (mì, tight / dense) plus 封 (to seal): to seal tightly so nothing leaks in or out. The word for airtight packaging, vacuum jars, and sealed envelopes.
面包	miàn bāo	bread — 面 miàn (flour) + 包 bāo (wrapped, bun). Literally "flour-bun." The general word for bread of the Western loaf type, as distinct from steamed 馒头 mántou.
面对	miàn duì	to face; to confront; to deal with — 面 (face) + 对 (to face; to be opposite to). Lit. "face-to-face with." To confront a reality, problem, or situation squarely rather than avoiding it. Widely used in motivational, psychological, and journalistic writing.
面前	miàn qián	in front of; before (someone); in one's presence — 面 miàn (face) + 前 qián (front). The space directly before one's face. Often used figuratively: 在困难面前 "in the face of difficulty," 在事实面前 "before the facts."
面容	miàn róng	countenance; the face
面条	miàn tiáo	noodles — The same 面 character. In northern China, 面 = wheat-flour dough → noodles. The flat, surface-like sheet of worked dough becomes strips (条 tiáo = strip). A vivid reminder that 面 means "surface/face" in the most general sense , the flat plane.
面子工程	miàn zi gōng chéng	Face engineering — Face engineering: infrastructure or projects built primarily for prestige rather than practical need. Empty airports in small cities, oversized government buildings, unnecessary highways: these are classic 面子工程.
描写	miáo xiě	to describe; to depict; to portray
渺小	miǎo xiǎo	insignificant; tiny before the vast
灭火	miè huǒ	to extinguish fire
民胞物与	mín bāo wù yǔ	all people are kin; all things are companions — universal fellowship — 民 (people) + 胞 (womb-siblings; kin) + 物 (things) + 与 (companions; associates). Zhang Zai's ethical derivation from 天人合一: if Heaven and Earth are the parents of all, then all human beings are kin born of the same parents, and all other things are our companions in this cosmic family.
民歌	míng ē	folk song — 民 + 歌 gē (song). A song that arises and circulates among the people rather than being composed for the concert hall: the traditional songs of a region or an ethnic group, often anonymous and passed down orally.
民间	mín jiān	among the people; folk; non-governmental — 民 + 间 jiān (among, within). The realm of ordinary life as opposed to the official, the courtly, or the state: that which exists among the people.
民间信仰	mín jiān xìn yǎng	folk religion
民权主义	Mín quán Zhǔ yì	Democracy — the rights and sovereignty of the people — Sun's vision of Chinese democracy combined Western constitutionalism with Chinese institutional traditions. The "Five-Power Constitution" added examination and control functions to the legislative-executive-judicial trifecta.
民生	mín shēng	the people's livelihood
民生主义	Mín shēng Zhǔ yì	People's Livelihood — economic justice and social welfare — The social-economic principle, influenced by land-value taxation theory and early socialism. Sun feared that China would develop capitalism's inequalities along with its productive power.
民心	mín xīn	the heart of the people
民众	mín zhòng	the masses; the general public — 民 + 众 zhòng (multitude, crowd). The ordinary public viewed as a large body, common in news writing and formal description: how the public reacts, what the public expects. More descriptive and less ideologically charged than 人民, and broader and more neutral than the warmer, address-style 大家.
民主	mín zhǔ	democracy; democratic — 民 mín (the people) + 主 zhǔ (master). The people as master, the modern term for democracy. Also used adjectivally: 民主国家 "a democratic country," 民主选举 "a democratic election."
民族	mín zú	ethnic group; nationality; a people — 民 + 族 zú (clan, lineage, group). A people considered as a cultural and ethnic stock: an ethnic group, a nationality, a nation in the cultural sense. China officially recognises 56 民族, the 汉族 Hànzú (Han) and 55 少数民族 shǎoshù mínzú (ethnic minorities).
民族主义	Mín zú Zhǔ yì	Nationalism — national identity and anti-imperialism — The first principle, evolving from anti-Manchu sentiment to pan-Chinese national identity to resistance against foreign imperialism. The evolution of this principle tracks the broader evolution of Chinese nationalism: from ethnic to civic, from anti-dynastic to anti-colonial.
闽南语	Mǐn nán yǔ	Southern Min , the Hokkien topolect spoken in southern Fujian, Taiwan (as 台語 Táiyǔ or 台灣話 Táiwānhuà), and across Southeast Asian Chinese communities in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and the Philippines.
敏感	mǐng ǎn	sensitive; highly responsive — 敏 mǐn (quick; alert; agile) + 感 gǎn (feel). Quick to feel. Used across registers: personality traits, skin types, and politically sensitive topics.
名辩	míng biàn	Mohist name-disputation
名词	míng cí	noun — 名 míng (name) + 词 cí (word). The "name-word," a noun: a word for a person, place, thing, or idea. 桌子, 北京, and 自由 are all 名词.
名次	míng cì	ranking; place
名分	míng fèn	name and duty — the obligation that comes with a title — 名 míng (name) + 分 fèn (portion, allotted duty). One's station and the obligations that station carries.
名家	Míng jiā	School of Names
名句	míng jù	a famous line; a well-known quotation — 名 míng (famous) + 句 jù (line). A celebrated line of verse or prose, so well known that it stands on its own apart from the work it came from. The pairing 千古名句 "a famous line for the ages" praises a line that has lasted.
名片	míng piàn	business card — 名 míng (name) + 片 piàn (flat slice; card). A "name slice" , the physical object that carries your name into another person's hand. Business card exchange in China carries ritual weight: present and receive with both hands, read the card before putting it away, never write on it.
名人	míng rén	famous person; celebrity; notable — 名 míng (name; fame) + 人 rén (person). A person whose name is widely known. Covers historical greats, contemporary celebrities, and anyone of notable standing. Context determines whether the register is elevated (historical figures) or casual (entertainers).
名声	míng shēng	reputation; standing (can be good or bad) — 名 míng (name) + 声 shēng (sound; voice; what is heard). What others say and hear about you , your name as it sounds in the world. Crucially neutral: 好名声 (good reputation) vs 坏名声 (bad reputation). The modifier does the moral work; 名声 itself simply denotes the fact of being talked about.
名实	míng shí	name and reality — the alignment that 正名 seeks — 名 míng (name) + 实 shí (reality, actuality). The pair names the problem: when 名 and 实 diverge, something false is being presented to the world. 名实相符 (name and reality correspond) is the condition 正名 aims to restore.
名望	míng wàng	fame; good standing; reputation — 名 míng (name) + 望 wàng (esteem). The fame and good repute a person enjoys: 很有名望 "to be of high standing." It blends being widely known with being respected, the regard attached to a name.
名誉	míng yù	reputation
名字	míng zi	name (personal name, general term) — 名 míng (name) + 字 zì (character; in classical usage, the courtesy name given at adulthood). In modern Mandarin, 名字 is the everyday word for a person's name , first name, full name, or nickname depending on context. Neutral register, universally usable.
明朝	míng cháo	Ming dynasty
明了	míng liǎo	to understand clearly
明亮	míng liàng	bright; luminous; well-lit — 明 míng + 亮 liàng (bright; shining). The compound for physical and figurative luminosity. Used for rooms, eyes, futures, and voices (a 明亮的嗓音 is a clear, bright singing voice).
明年	míng nián	next year — 明 míng + 年 nián (year). The same "bright/coming" sense extended to years. Pattern: 明天 tomorrow · 明年 next year · 明月 the bright moon (classical). The character 明 reaches across all timescales.
明前茶	míng qián chá	pre-Qingming tea — the highest harvest grade
明确	míng qu è	clear and definite; explicit; to specify — 明 míng + 确 què (definite; certain; firm). Used for rules, policies, goals, and instructions that leave no room for ambiguity. More formal than 明白. 请明确你的要求 = "Please specify your requirements."
明堂	míng táng	Bright hall — Bright hall: the open space in front of a geomantically ideal site, where qi gathers before the building. The concept appears in both palace architecture and burial site theory.
明天	míng tiān	tomorrow — 明 míng (bright; dawn; the next) + 天 tiān (day). The "bright day," the day the sun will rise again. 明 also means "next" in 明年 míngnián (next year) and 明月 míngyuè (the bright moon, a poetic image for longing). Note: in classical Chinese, 明日 míngrì is the literary form; 明天 is modern spoken Mandarin.
明天会下雨	míng tiān huì xià yǔ	it will rain tomorrow — 会 as future/likelihood marker — 会 has a second major function entirely distinct from learned ability: expressing expectation, likelihood, or prediction about a future event. This 会 does not mean "has learned how to" , rain cannot "learn" to rain. Instead, it signals the speaker's confident expectation that something will occur.
明天就到了	míng tiān jiù dào le	arrives as soon as tomorrow; it'll be here by tomorrow already — 就 can also point toward an imminent future event, expressing that something will happen sooner than might be expected. The speaker's attitude: "it's coming up fast, it'll be here before you know it." This future-pointing 就 often co-occurs with 了 at the sentence end.
明显	míng xiǎn	obvious; evident; marked — 明 míng + 显 xiǎn (to show; visible; eminent). What is bright is also visible to all. Used when something is undeniably apparent: improvement, change, a lie. 明显进步 "marked improvement."
明星	míng xīng	star (celebrity) — 明 (bright) + 星: the bright star, classical Chinese for Venus before it became the word for screen and stage fame. 追星 ("chasing stars") is fandom, and a 粉丝 (fěnsī, fan, a sound-loan that also means glass noodles) does the chasing.
明智	míng zhì	wise; sensible; showing good judgment — 明 míng (clear, bright) + 智 zhì (wisdom; intelligence). A bright mind, one that sees clearly. The compliment given to good decisions, prudent actions. 这是个明智的选择 "That is a wise choice."
命苦	mìng kǔ	hard fate; to have a bitter lot in life
命令	mìng lìng	to order; an order, a directive — 命 plus 令 lìng (order). A synonym-compound: both characters mean "command," doubled for clarity. Used for formal, top-down orders in military, governmental, and parental contexts. Cooler in tone than 让 ràng (to let, to make) and harder than 要求 yāoqiú (to request).
模样	mú yàng	looks; appearance
陌生	mò shēng	unfamiliar; strange; unknown — 陌 mò (a stranger; a path between rice fields, where you encounter people you don't know) + 生 shēng (unprocessed; unfamiliar). For unfamiliar places, strangers, and new experiences. 陌生人 = stranger. 对我来说很陌生 = "It's unfamiliar to me."
陌生人	mò shēng rén	stranger
墨家	Mò jiā	Mohism — universal love, opposition to aggressive war — Founded by 墨子 Mòzǐ (c. 470–391 BCE). Distinguished by: 兼爱 jiān'ài (impartial concern for all, not just one's own family and state), 非攻 fēi gōng (opposition to offensive war), and a utilitarian standard of moral judgment (actions are good if they benefit the people materially).
墨经	Mò Jīng	the Mohist Canon — logic and proto-science — The 墨经 consists of four chapters within the 墨子 (经上, 经下, 经说上, 经说下) and represents the most systematic engagement with formal reasoning, optics, mechanics, and geometric principles in pre-Han Chinese thought. The Canon defines terms, categorizes knowledge claims, and argues from evidence.
墨子	Mò zǐ	Master Mo; the person and the text — The name refers both to the historical philosopher (c. 470–391 BCE) and to the text compiled by his followers. The 墨子 consists of 71 chapters (of which 53 survive), covering ethics, political philosophy, logic, and the 墨经 (the scientific and logical canons).
默读	mò dú	to read silently — 默 mò (silent) + 读. The marked term for silent reading , marked precisely because the unmarked sense of 读 is voiced. A reading classroom may instruct students 先默读，再朗读 "first read silently, then aloud."
默认	mò rèn	to tacitly acknowledge; (computing) default — 默 mò (silent) + 认 rèn. Silent acknowledgment , agreeing by not objecting, acquiescing without explicit confirmation. In computing and modern Chinese tech vocabulary, the same word means "default": 默认设置 mòrèn shèzhì = "default settings."
母鸡	mǔ jī	hen — 母 (female) + 鸡 (chicken). The egg-laying hen; a 母鸡下蛋 (the hen lays eggs) is the first farmyard fact every child learns.
母亲河	mǔ qīn hé	Mother River , the affectionate designation for the Yellow River, emphasizing its role as the origin of Chinese agricultural civilization. The Yangtze also claims this title in southern China, but the Yellow River carries the deeper historical weight.
母语	mǔ yǔ	mother tongue; first language — 母 mǔ (mother) + 语 yǔ (language). Mother tongue , the language absorbed in childhood, tied to family and home. 母语为汉语的人 = native Chinese speakers. 母语习得 = first language acquisition. 目标语 mùbiāoyǔ = target language (the language being learned). 外语 wàiyǔ = foreign language.
木耳	mù ěr	wood ear fungus; cloud ear mushroom — 木 (wood, tree) + 耳 (ear-handle). The edible black fungus Auricularia auricula-judae , named for its resemblance to a wooden vessel's ear-handle. A staple of Chinese cooking, added to stir-fries and soups for its chewy texture.
木卡姆	Mù kǎ mǔ	The Uyghur Muqam , twelve suites of music incorporating song, instrumental performance, and dance, each built on a distinct modal system. A living art form and UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, the Muqam is considered the highest expression of Uyghur musical culture.
木马	mù mǎ	wooden horse; vaulting horse; trojan — 木 (wood) + 马 (horse). A horse made of wood: the rocking toy, the gymnastics vaulting horse, and the computer 木马 (a trojan), all named for the most famous wooden horse of all, the one at Troy (特洛伊木马).
木头	mù tou	wood; timber; (of a person) wooden, dull — 木 mù (wood, tree) + 头 tou (suffix). Wood as a material. Used figuratively of a person who is slow or unresponsive: 木头人 "a blockhead," literally a wooden person.
目标	mù biāo	goal; target
目标价	mù biāo jià	target price — Naming your target moves the discussion from "lower" to "can you reach this." Give it with a reason, such as a retail price point or a competing quote (另一家的报价 lìng yì jiā de bàojià), without naming the other factory.
目光	mù guāng	gaze; line of sight; vision (figurative) — 目 (eye) + 光 (light). The light from the eye , the gaze as something projected. Used both literally (眼中的目光, the look in someone's eyes) and figuratively (目光短浅 mùguāng duǎnqiǎn, short-sighted vision; 目光长远 mùguāng chángyuǎn, far-sighted).
目连	Mù lián	Mulian (Maudgalyāyana), the filial monk
目录	mù lù	table of contents; catalogue; directory — 目 (eye; item) + 录 (record, to record). The document your eye scans to locate content. 书的目录 (book's table of contents); 图书目录 (library catalogue); 产品目录 (product catalogue).
目前	mù qián	at present; currently
墓地	mù dì	cemetery; grave site
拿出来	ná chū lái	to take out; to produce; to bring out — 拿 ná (take; hold; grasp) + 出来 chūlái (bring out). To produce something from a container, pocket, bag, or interior , making it visible to the speaker. Also used abstractly: 拿出证据 (produce evidence), 拿出方案 (put forward a plan). The 出来 marks the transition from concealed to revealed.
哪里	nǎ lǐ	where; (modest deflection) — 哪 (nǎ, which) + 里 = 哪里 (which interior zone, where). Beyond literal location questions, 哪里 doubles as a stock modest deflection: when someone praises you, responding 哪里哪里 (nǎlǐ nǎlǐ, literally "where, where?") means "oh, not at all, you're too kind." The deflection works because 哪里 implies the prais…
哪里哪里	nǎ lǐ nǎ lǐ	"where, where?" — the classic deflection of a compliment; "you flatter me" — The quintessential 谦虚 response to a compliment , a rhetorical question that denies the existence of the praised quality. Literally "where is this quality you're seeing?" The doubling intensifies the deflection.
那个	nà ge	that one — "Uh…" or "that…" The single most common verbal filler in Mandarin, used to stall for half a second while the next word arrives. Stretched out as 那个… 那个… it functions almost identically to English "um." Overusing it sounds hesitant; sprinkling it in sounds native.
那就这样吧	nà jiù zhè yàng ba	"Okay, let's leave it at that — "Okay, let's leave it at that." The standard wrap-up marker. Signals that the conversation has reached a natural stopping point and you are about to close. The 吧 invites the other party to agree to wind down.
那里	nà lǐ	there
那时候	nà shí hou	at that time
那样	nà yàng	that way
奶牛	nǎi niú	dairy cow
耐心	nài xīn	patience
男孩	nán hái	boy — 男 (male) plus 孩 (child). Often expanded to 男孩子 (nánháizi) with no change in meaning. Used for boys and, loosely, for young men.
男朋友	nán péng you	boyfriend: a male romantic partner — 男 nán (male) + 朋友 péngyou (friend). The standard word for a boyfriend; 女朋友 nǚ péngyou is the matching girlfriend. The 朋友 base shows how the modern romantic term grew out of the plain word for companion.
男性	nán xìng	male; men (as a category) — 男 nán (man) + 性 xìng (sex). The male sex, men considered as a category: 成年男性 "adult males," 男性朋友 "a male friend." The formal counterpart to 女性, used wherever one speaks of men as a group rather than addressing a particular man.
男子汉	nán zǐ hàn	a real man; a manly man — 男子 nánzǐ (male, man) + 汉 hàn (fellow). A man in the sense of courage and backbone, the one who keeps his word and bears hardship. 男子汉大丈夫 "a true man and great fellow" is the full heroic flourish.
南北	nán běi	north-south
南方	nán fāng	the South; southern China — 南 (south) + 方 (direction; region). In Chinese cultural geography, 南方 (the South) and 北方 (the North) mark one of the most significant cultural divides in the country: the Yangtze River (扬子江) and the Qinling-Huai River line are the approximate cultural boundary.
南京	Nán jīng	Nanjing (city) — 南 (south) + 京 (capital). The Southern Capital , the counterpart to 北京 Běijīng (Northern Capital). Nanjing served as the Ming dynasty capital from 1368 to 1421, before Yongle moved the court north.
南人	Nán rén	Southerners — fourth class — Former Southern Song subjects, the last conquered and most numerous. Faced highest taxes, most restricted access to office, forbidden from owning weapons. Approximately 85% of the Yuan's total population.
南无阿弥陀佛	Ná mó Ē mí tuó fó	I take refuge in Amitābha Buddha
南无观音菩萨	Nā mó Guān yīn Pú sà	the invocation — "homage to Guanyin Bodhisattva" — 南无 nāmó is the Chinese rendering of Sanskrit namas (homage, refuge). The full invocation 南无观音菩萨 is spoken at times of fear, suffering, gratitude, or supplication. It requires no ritual setting, no clergy, no formal initiation.
难题	nán tí	hard problem; knotty issue; difficult question — 难 nán (difficult) + 题 tí (problem). A problem that resists easy solution, whether on paper or in life: 出了一道难题 "posed a tough problem." A close cousin is 习题 xítí, the practice exercises a student works through.
脑力	nǎo lì	mental effort
闹洞房	nào dòng fáng	The wedding-night hazing — The wedding-night hazing: guests entering the bridal chamber to subject the couple to games and pranks. The custom is ancient, widely practiced, and occasionally criticized for going too far. The word 闹 (nào) means to make noise, to create commotion.
内部	nèi bù	internal; the interior; inside (of an organization) — 内 nèi (inside) + 部 bù (section). The inner part of a body, machine, or group, often the confidential inside of an organization: 内部消息 "inside information," 内部会议 "an internal meeting." Its pair is 外部 wàibù (external).
内功	nèi gōng	internal martial cultivation
内家拳	nèi jiā quán	internal martial arts — 内 nèi (internal) + 家 jiā (school; tradition) + 拳 quán (fist; boxing). The internal arts (Taijiquan 太极拳, Baguazhang 八卦掌, Xingyiquan 形意拳) emphasize cultivation of internal energy (气 qì), sensitivity, and relaxed power over brute muscular force.
内容	nèi róng	content; what is contained
内心	nèi xīn	inner heart; deepest feelings; the inner self — 内 nèi (inside; inner) + 心 xīn (heart). The deepest, most private layer of a person's interior life, what they feel before they decide how to present it to the world. Common in introspective prose, therapeutic contexts, and literary characterization. 内心世界 = the inner world.
内行	nèi háng	expert; insider; one who knows the trade — 内 nèi (inside) + 行 háng. Inside-the-row. Someone who is inside the trade , knows its tools, its standards, its tells. The opposite is 外行 wàiháng "outside-the-row," an outsider or amateur. 这件事我是外行 = "I'm a layperson on this." 一看就是内行 = "you can tell at a glance he's an expert."
能工巧匠	néng gōng qiǎo jiàng	skilled craftsmen
能力	néng lì	ability; capability; capacity — 能 néng (be able) + 力 lì (strength). The general word for ability, what a person is capable of doing: 工作能力 "work ability," 有能力 "to be capable."
能量	néng liàng	Energy — Energy. Physics term and self-help term alike: 正能量 (positive energy) is the government-endorsed phrase for uplifting content, a usage physicists did not authorize.
你吃了吗	nǐ chī le ma	have you eaten? (intimate register)
你好	nǐ hǎo	hello (formal register)
你好吗	nǐ hǎo ma	how are you? (borrowed register)
你好意思	nǐ hǎo yì si	you have the nerve / how shameless of you
你们	nǐ men	you (plural)
你认真的吗	nǐ rèn zhēn de ma	are you serious? are you for real?
你什么意思？	nǐ shén me yì si	What do you mean? / What are you implying? — Can be a neutral request for clarification or a challenging, slightly confrontational demand , "what exactly are you getting at?" Tone of voice and context determine everything.
你说嘛	nǐ shuō ma	just say it / tell me then (urging)
你在做什么？	nǐ zài zuò shén me ?	What are you doing? — The standard colloquial question for asking what someone is currently doing. 在 alone (not 正在) is the norm in this question. 你正在做什么？is grammatical but sounds slightly unnatural or formal in casual conversation. The question naturally invites a 在/正在 answer.
你知道吗	nǐ zhī dào ma	"You know?" Functions like English "you know?" both as a sincere check-in and as discourse filler. Useful for keeping the listener engaged mid-sentence. Overused in casual conversation by younger speakers, where it can become as habitual as English "like."
年代	nián dài	decade; period
年龄	nián líng	age; years of life — 年 nián (year) + 龄 líng (age; years of life , used specifically for age of living things). The formal word for a person's age. 年龄段 niánlíng duàn = age group. 适龄 shìlíng = of appropriate age (e.g., 适龄儿童 school-age children).
年轻	nián qīng	young — 年 nián (year; age) + 轻 qīng (light; young; not heavy). The standard adjective for "young" , the opposite of 老 lǎo. 年轻人 niánqīngrén = young people. 年轻化 niánqīnghuà = to become younger/more youthful. 越活越年轻 "getting younger as I live" , a compliment to someone who looks youthful.
年夜饭	nián yè fàn	New Year's Eve reunion dinner — the most important meal of the year — 年 nián (year) + 夜 yè (night/eve) + 饭 fàn (meal). The reunion dinner on New Year's Eve, the sacred center of Spring Festival. Every family member is expected to return home for this meal, regardless of distance.
念佛	niàn fó	Buddha-recitation — the primary and most accessible practice — 念 niàn (to recite; to think of; to hold in mind) + 佛 fó (Buddha). The recitation of Amitābha's name, 南无阿弥陀佛 Nāmó Āmítuófó ("homage to Amitābha Buddha"), as a continuous practice.
念书	niàn shū	to read aloud; to study; to attend school
念头	niàn tou	a thought; an idea; an intention (that arises)
念珠	niàn zhū	recitation beads (mala)
涅槃重生	niè pán chóng shēng	to be reborn through the fire; the modern metaphor
您的意思是	nín de yì si shì	what you mean is — Restating what you heard is the most powerful check you have, because it forces a yes or no on your version. 我理解的是……对吗 ("my understanding is ..., right?") does the same job. 也就是说 (yě jiù shì shuō, "in other words") works mid-conversation.
宁可	nìng kě	would rather (at a cost)
牛逼	niú bī	badass, awesome (vulgar)
牛角	niú jiǎo	cow horn
牛奶	niú nǎi	milk (cow's) — 牛 (ox/cow) + 奶 (nǎi, milk/breast). The default word for drinking milk in Mandarin; 奶 alone leans toward breast milk or the act of nursing, so the 牛 makes the source explicit.
牛年	niú nián	Year of the Ox
牛排	niú pái	steak — 牛 (ox) + 排 (pái, a slab/cutlet, from 排骨 spare-rib). A Western-style cut of beef cooked as one piece, ordered by doneness the way English orders rare to well-done.
牛肉	niú ròu	beef — 牛 (ox) + 肉 (ròu, meat). Chinese names meat by its animal, so beef is literally ox-meat, parallel to 猪肉 (zhūròu, pork) and 鸡肉 (jīròu, chicken).
牛仔	niú zǎi	cowboy
牛仔裤	niú zǎi kù	jeans — 牛仔 (niúzǎi, cowboy, literally ox-lad) + 裤 (kù, trousers). The denim of the American cowboy, named in Chinese after the herder himself.
农场	nóng chǎng	farm — 农 (farming) plus 场 (ground, site). A working farm as an enterprise, larger and more organized than a single household plot.
农村	nóng cūn	countryside, rural area — 农 (farming) plus 村 (village). The rural world as a whole, the standing opposite of 城市 (chéngshì, the city) in any discussion of Chinese society.
农夫	nóng fū	farmer; a man of the land — 农 nóng (agriculture, farming) + 夫 fū (man). A man who works the land, the farmer in a plain, somewhat literary or old-fashioned key. It pictures the individual tiller rather than the peasantry as a social class, and turns up often in fables and proverbs about country life.
农历	nóng lì	the lunar calendar — 农 (farming) plus 历 (calendar). The traditional lunisolar calendar, named for farmers because its solar terms tell you when to plant and harvest. 春节 (chūnjié) falls on 农历 New Year.
农民	nóng mín	farmer, peasant — 农 (farming) plus 民 (the common people). A person whose work and household registration are agricultural. In modern China it also marks a social and administrative category, not only an occupation.
农民起义	nóng mín qǐ yì	peasant uprising
农业	nóng yè	agriculture; farming — 农 nóng (farming) + 业 yè (sector). The agricultural sector: 农业生产 "agricultural production," 农业大国 "a major agricultural country." The oldest of the great 业 in Chinese economic thought, long held as the root on which all else rests.
农作物	nóng zuò wù	crops — 农 (farming) plus 作物 (cultivated plant). The cultivated crops themselves: grain, cotton, vegetables, anything grown on purpose for harvest.
弄错	nòng cuò	to get wrong; mix up
努力	nǔ lì	to make an effort; to strive; hardworking — 努 nǔ (to put forth) + 力 lì (effort). To bend one's strength toward a goal, the everyday word for trying hard: 努力工作 "to work hard," 努力学习 "to study diligently." Works as both verb and noun.
女儿	nǚ ér	daughter — 女 nǚ (female) + 儿 ér (child; son , used neutrally here). Daughter. The contrast with 儿子 érzi (son , lit.
女孩	nǚ hái	girl — 女 (female) plus 孩 (child). Like 男孩, it freely takes the extra 子 as 女孩子. It covers girls and, in everyday speech, young women.
女朋友	nǚ péng you	girlfriend
女王	nǚ wáng	queen (regnant)
女性	nǚ xìng	female; women (as a category) — 女 nǚ (woman) + 性 xìng (sex). The female sex, women considered as a category or class: 职业女性 "professional women," 女性用品 "products for women." More formal and collective than 女人, the way one refers to women in writing, statistics, and public discourse.
排队	pái duì	to line up, to queue — 排 (to arrange in a row) + 队 (a formed line). The verb every visitor learns first: to stand one behind another and wait your turn.
排练	pái liàn	to rehearse
排他	pái tā	exclusive; to exclude others
派出所	pài chū suǒ	local police substation; community police office
盼望	pàn wàng	to look forward to; to long for eagerly — 盼 pàn (to long for, to expect) + 望 wàng (to look toward). To wait eagerly and warmly for something one cares about: 盼望已久 "long looked forward to." More emotional and yearning than 希望, it suggests an active, heartfelt waiting.
旁人	páng rén	bystanders; those on the sidelines (literary) — 旁 páng (side; beside) + 人 rén. Literally "people at the side": observers, onlookers, those not directly involved in a situation. The word carries a slightly theatrical quality: you, the protagonist, and 旁人 who watch. More literary than 别人. Common in classical and modern literary prose.
跑步	pǎo bù	to jog; to run (as exercise); a run — 跑 + 步 (bù, step). The everyday verb-noun for running as exercise. Used both as an activity (我每天跑步, "I jog every day") and as a noun (一次跑步, "one running session"). The word covers everything from a casual neighborhood jog to marathon training.
跑出来	pǎo chū lái	to run out (toward speaker) — 跑 pǎo (run) + 出来 chūlái (come out). The full directional compound: running out of an enclosed space toward the speaker's position. The 来 anchors orientation , the speaker is outside, watching the emergence happen.
跑道	pǎo dào	running track; runway (airport); a course of action — 跑 + 道 (dào, road; way; track). The physical track for running, the airport runway for planes, and , figuratively , a chosen course of professional or personal direction. 选择新的跑道 ("to choose a new track") is a near-fixed metaphor in career writing.
跑了	pǎo le	got away; ran off; (of fish, opportunity) escaped — 跑 + 了 (le, perfective particle). A small but very common construction marking that something or someone has escaped or slipped away. The subject is often something one wanted to keep: a thief, a debtor, a fish, a customer, an opportunity.
跑腿	pǎo tuǐ	to run errands
泡茶	pào chá	to brew tea; to steep tea — 泡 pào (to soak; to steep; to foam) + 茶 chá (tea). The everyday verb for making tea. 你喝什么茶？我去泡 "What tea would you like? I'll go steep it." Also: 泡茶时间 steeping time · 第一泡 the first infusion.
配角	pèi ju é	supporting role
朋友圈	péng you quān	circle of friends; WeChat Moments
皮蛋	pí dàn	century egg, preserved egg — 皮 (pí, skin) + 蛋: a duck egg cured in lime, ash, and salt until the white turns to dark amber jelly and the yolk to creamy green-grey. The leathery surface gives it the "skin" name.
疲困	pí kùn	tired and hard-pressed
脾气	pí qi	temper
脾性	pí xìng	disposition; temperament
匹夫	pǐ fū	a common man
偏见	piān jiàn	prejudice, bias
漂亮的花	piào liang de huā	beautiful flower — adjective + 的 + noun — The most basic use of 的: an adjective modifying a noun. In this pattern, 的 functions like the English suffix "-'s" or the phrase "that is." 漂亮的花 = the flower that is beautiful = the beautiful flower.
拼命	pīn mìng	to risk one's life; to do something with everything one has — 拼 pīn (to throw together; to stake) plus 命. To "stake one's life" on something, used both literally (combat, rescue) and figuratively for any effort given without holding back. 拼命工作 "to work like one's life depends on it" is the standard phrase for sustained, all-in effort.
拼音	pīn yīn	Pinyin; the phonetic spelling of Mandarin — 拼 pīn (to piece together) + 音 yīn (sound). The Romanized spelling that pieces a Mandarin syllable from initial, final, and tone. The scaffolding every learner climbs before the characters take hold.
贫富	pín fù	poor and rich; wealth gap
贫困	pín kùn	poverty; impoverished — 贫 (poor) + 困 (hard-pressed). Poverty seen as a wall that pens people in: not merely low income, but the trapped condition want creates. Formal register, common in policy and reporting.
品德	pǐn dé	moral character; the virtue a person has — 品 pǐn (rank; quality; character) + 德 dé. The grade of one's virtue. Where 道德 is morality in general, 品德 is the moral quality of a particular person. 品德高尚 "of lofty character" is the standard praise; 品德败坏 "of degraded character" is the standard condemnation.
品格	pǐng é	character; moral caliber
品牌	pǐn pái	brand
平安	píng ān	safe and sound; at peace; well — 平 píng (calm) + 安 ān (safe). Safe and well, free of harm or trouble: 一路平安 "have a safe trip," 平安回家 "to get home safely." A staple of blessings and farewells.
平常	píng cháng	ordinary; common; usually, ordinarily — 平 píng (level; plain) + 常 cháng (ordinary). Both an adjective (unremarkable, common) and a time word (in ordinary times, usually): 平常的一天 "an ordinary day," 我平常六点起床 "I usually get up at six."
平地	píng dì	level ground; flat land — 平 píng (level) + 地 dì (ground). Flat, even land, as opposed to slopes or mountains: 一片平地 "a stretch of level ground." The opposite is hilly or broken terrain.
平等	píng děng	equality; equal in status — 平 píng (level) + 等 děng (rank). Equal standing, no rank set above another: 人人平等 "everyone is equal," 男女平等 "equality of men and women." More about status than about fairness in dealings.
平凡	píng fán	commonplace
平房	píng fáng	single-storey house
平衡	píng héng	balance; equilibrium
平静	píng jìng	calm; tranquil
平均	píng jūn	average; on average; to even out — 平 píng (even) + 均 jūn (equal). The arithmetic mean, the level reached when a total is shared out evenly: 平均分 "average score," 平均年龄 "average age," 平均分配 "to distribute evenly."
平面	píng miàn	flat surface; plane; two-dimensional — 平 píng (flat) + 面 miàn (surface; face). A flat surface, and in geometry a plane. Also the modifier in 平面设计 píngmiàn shèjì "graphic design," the flat, two-dimensional kind.
平民	píng mín	commoner; an ordinary person (vs the elite) — 平 píng (level, ordinary, common) + 民. An ordinary person without rank, wealth, or official position: the commoner as opposed to nobles, officials, or celebrities. 平民百姓 píngmín bǎixìng is a fixed pairing meaning the common folk, the man and woman in the street.
平稳	píng wěn	steady; smooth; stable — 平 píng (level) + 稳 wěn (steady; firm). Moving or sitting on an even keel, without jolts or swings: 平稳着陆 "a smooth landing," 物价平稳 "prices are stable."
评价	píng jià	to appraise; an evaluation, review — 评 (to judge, comment) + 价 (worth). To weigh something and assign it a worth: a teacher's assessment, a customer's review, a verdict on a person's conduct. Works as both verb and noun.
评论	píng lùn	to review, to comment; a review, a commentary — 评 píng (to appraise, to judge) + 论. To pass critical judgement on something, or the resulting commentary. A film review, a book review, a comment posted under an article (评论区 pínglùnqū "the comments section") are all 评论.
凭借	píng jiè	rely on, by virtue of
破坏	pò huài	to destroy, to undermine — 破 (to break, smash) + 坏 (to ruin). Two near-synonyms doubled for force. Destroys physical things (buildings, environment) and abstract ones alike (trust, an atmosphere, a plan, the rules).
菩萨心肠	pú sà xīn cháng	a bodhisattva's heart; saintly compassion — 心肠 xīncháng = the heart-and-gut, the moral center of a person. 菩萨心肠 describes someone of exceptional compassion and forgiveness , a person who cannot bear to see others suffer and who gives without calculation.
浦东	Pǔ dōng	Pudong — Pudong: the eastern bank of the Huangpu River and its hinterland, designated a special economic development zone in 1990. Its skyline of supertall towers built since the 1990s is the visual symbol of reform-era China.
普通	pǔ tōng	ordinary; common; general; average — 普 pǔ (widespread; universal) + 通 (general; running throughout). Widespread and holding everywhere: the quality of being ordinary, the common case rather than the special one. 普通人 (an ordinary person), 普通话 (the common spoken standard, Mandarin).
普陀山	Pǔ tuó shān	Putuoshan (Guanyin's sacred island)
七情	qī qíng	the seven emotions
七情六欲	qī qíng liù yù	the seven emotions and six desires; the full range of human feeling — 七情 (the seven emotions: joy, anger, sorrow, fear, love, aversion, desire) + 六欲 (the six desires of the senses). Together they name the complete inner life of a human being.
七夕	qī xī	the Qixi Festival; the Chinese Valentine's Day — 七 qī + 夕 xī (evening). The seventh evening of the seventh lunar month, the annual meeting of the Weaver Girl (织女) and the Cowherd (牛郎). Once a women's festival for praying for skill in needlework (乞巧, "begging for cleverness"), it is now celebrated as a day for lovers.
七月	qī yu è	July; the seventh month — 七 qī + 月 yuè (month). July in the solar calendar. The seventh lunar month is the Ghost Month (鬼月), when the gates of the underworld are believed to open and spirits roam among the living; its fifteenth day is the Ghost Festival (中元节).
妻子	qī zi	wife — 妻 qī (wife) + 子 zi (suffix). The standard modern word for wife. Note the tone: in classical Chinese 妻子 qīzǐ meant "wife and children," but the modern toneless reading qīzi means the wife alone.
期间	qī jiān	period; during the time of — 期 qī (a fixed period) + 间 jiān (interval). A defined stretch of time, often used after an event to mean "during": 假期期间 "during the holidays," 会议期间 "in the course of the meeting."
期望	qī wàng	to expect; expectation; to set hopes on — 期 qī (a set time, to anticipate) + 望 wàng (to look toward). To expect something of someone or some outcome, with a definite hope and often a standard behind it: 不要辜负大家的期望 "do not let down everyone's expectations." Weightier and more formal than 希望.
齐国	Qí Guó	the state of Qi — first hegemon's domain
齐桓公与管仲	Qí Huán Gōng yǔ Guǎn Zhòng	Duke Huan of Qi and Guan Zhong — the classical model of ruler and reforming minister — 齐桓公 Qí Huán Gōng (r. 685–643 BCE) became the dominant power of the early Spring and Autumn through the administrative genius of his minister 管仲 Guǎn Zhòng. The partnership became the canonical Chinese example of a ruler who provides authority and a minister who provides competence.
齐全	qí quán	complete (in range); all there; fully stocked — 齐 qí (even; all present) + 全 quán (complete). Said of a set or selection where every needed item is on hand: 设备齐全 "fully equipped," 品种齐全 "a complete range of varieties." Stresses that nothing in the expected range is missing.
其次	qí cì	secondly; next; then — 其 qí (that; those) + 次 cì (order; rank; next). "Next in that sequence" , used to introduce the second point in a ranked list, following 首先 shǒuxiān (first of all) or 第一 dì yī. Slightly more formal than 然后 ránhòu, which is purely sequential.
其他	qí tā	other; the rest; others — 其 qí (that; those) + 他 tā (other). "Those others" , anything outside the named set. The variant 其它 qítā uses the non-human 它 and is preferred when referring to things rather than people, though in practice 其他 covers both.
其它	qí tā	other; the rest (of things)
其余	qí yú	the rest; the remainder; the others — 其 qí (those) + 余 yú (remainder; surplus; what is left). "Those that remain" , refers to everything in a set that has not already been specified. More formal than 其他; 其余 often implies a complete remainder (everything else), while 其他 may just mean "various others."
其中	qí zhōng	among them; within; therein — 其 qí (its; that) + 中 zhōng (middle; within). "Within that" or "among them" , used to pick out elements from a previously named set. One of the most frequent formal connectives in written Chinese, where English might say "of these" or "among which."
骑马	qí mǎ	to ride a horse
企业	qǐ yè	enterprise; firm; company (as an organization) — 企 qǐ (to stand on tiptoe; to aspire) + 业 yè (undertaking). A business organization: 国有企业 "state-owned enterprise," 私营企业 "private enterprise," 企业家 "entrepreneur." The standard term for a firm as a legal and economic body.
起草	qǐ cǎo	to draft (a document); to draw up — 起 qǐ (to begin; to raise) + 草 cǎo (draft). To compose the first version of a formal text, a contract, law, speech, or plan. 起草合同 "to draft a contract."
起订量	qǐ dìng liàng	minimum order quantity (MOQ) — "Order-starting quantity," often per colour or per SKU rather than per order. Ask which. Factories will usually trade a lower MOQ for a higher unit price.
起飞	qǐ fēi	to take off — 起 (to rise) plus 飞 (to fly): to rise into flight. Used literally of aircraft leaving the runway and figuratively of an economy or career that is about to surge.
起义	qǐ yì	righteous uprising; revolutionary revolt — 起 (to rise; to stand up) + 义 (righteousness). The act of rising against an unjust authority, with 义 marking the moral legitimacy of the act. In Chinese historiography and political vocabulary, 起义 is the standard term for revolts understood as righteous from the inside.
起因	qǐ yīn	the cause; what set something off — 起 qǐ (to rise; to start) + 因 yīn (cause). The cause that started a chain of events, the spark that set a matter in motion: 事情的起因 "the origin of the matter."
气场	qì chǎng	aura; energy field; presence (modern slang) — 气 qì + 场 chǎng (field, as in electromagnetic field or a venue). Originally a TCM and qigong term for the field of qi that radiates from a practitioner. Absorbed into popular culture as a way of describing the palpable aura of a charismatic person. 气场强 = powerful aura; 气场弱 = weak presence.
气愤	qì fèn	indignant; righteously angry — 气 qì + 愤 fèn (indignation; righteous anger, from the image of qi pressing against the heart). Slightly stronger and more formal than 生气. Implies that the anger is justified, that you are responding to something genuinely unfair or wrong. Less colloquial, more dignified.
气候	qì hòu	climate; the long-term atmospheric pattern — 气 qì + 候 hòu (season; to wait; signs). 候 originally referred to the five-day intervals used in classical Chinese to track seasonal changes. 气候 is the patterned behavior of atmospheric qi over time: climate, not weather. Also used metaphorically: 政治气候 (political climate).
气色	qì sè	complexion; appearance of health (lit. "qi-color") — 气 qì + 色 sè (color; appearance). In TCM, the complexion (the color and quality of the face) is a direct index of the health of one's internal qi. 气色好 (good complexion) = qi is ample and circulating freely; 气色差 (poor complexion) = qi is deficient or blocked. A doctor's first diagnostic tool.
气势	qì shì	momentum; imposing presence; force of spirit — 气 qì + 势 shì (power; momentum; force, the potential energy of a situation). The directed force of qi, outward projection of power rather than inner refinement (气质). An army, a waterfall, a master calligrapher's brushstroke, a confident leader entering a room: all can have 气势.
气死了	qì sǐ le	furious; livid
气温	qì wēn	air temperature — 气 qì (air; atmospheric qi) + 温 wēn (warmth; temperature). The temperature of the air, a meteorological and everyday term. Used in weather reports, health advice, and daily conversation about the feel of a day.
气血	qì xu è	qi and blood
气韵	qì yùn	spirit resonance; vital rhythm — 气 qì (breath; vital energy) + 韵 yùn (resonance; rhyme; musical tone). The first and supreme of Xie He's Six Principles: 气韵生动 qìyùn shēngdòng, "spirit resonance, life movement." A painting that has 气韵 is alive; one that lacks it is mere skilled craft.
气韵生动	qì yùn shēng dòng	spirit resonance and vitality — the supreme aesthetic criterion — Spirit resonance, life movement , Xie He first principle of painting, and the supreme criterion by which Chinese paintings are judged. A work with 气韵生动 has a quality of living presence that cannot be reduced to technical competence. It is the highest praise in Chinese art criticism.
气质	qì zhì	temperament; elegant bearing; innate quality — 气 qì + 质 zhì (substance; essence; nature). The essential quality of a person's qi, their innate temperament and the bearing it produces. In psychological Chinese, it corresponds to personality type. In everyday speech, 有气质 means "has an air about them": elegant, distinctive, refined.
恰当	qià dàng	apt; fitting
千古	qiāng ǔ	through all the ages; eternal; (of the dead) for ever — 千 qiān + 古 gǔ (antiquity; old). All the ages of history, time out of mind. 千古名句 is a line famous through the ages; 千古罪人 (a sinner for all time) is someone whose crime history will never forget.
千里	qiān lǐ	a thousand li; a great distance — 千 qiān + 里 lǐ (the Chinese mile). Literally a thousand li, but in practice any great distance. 千里迢迢 qiānlǐ tiáotiáo describes a long, arduous journey from far away.
千里迢迢	qiān lǐ tiáo tiáo	from a thousand li away; across a great distance — 千里 (a thousand li) + 迢迢 (tiáotiáo, remote, far off , a reduplication conveying long distance and weariness). The compound evokes a journey undertaken across great distance with effort and determination.
千里缘	qiān lǐ yuán	a connection across a thousand miles; long-distance destined bond — 千里 qiānlǐ = a thousand li (the traditional Chinese unit of distance; figuratively: any great distance). The phrase evokes connections that transcend physical separation , the meeting of people from far apart who nonetheless find each other.
千里之行	qiān lǐ zhī xíng	a journey of a thousand li
千秋	qiān qiū	a thousand autumns; the ages; eternity — 千 qiān + 秋 qiū (autumn, here standing for a year). A thousand years, hence the long span of history and posterity. 千秋万代 (a thousand autumns, ten thousand generations) means for all time, down all future ages. 名垂千秋 is to have one's name endure through the ages.
千万	qiān wàn	ten million; by all means; absolutely (must / must not) — 千 qiān (thousand) + 万 wàn (ten-thousand), literally ten million. But its most common use is adverbial and emphatic, urging or warning with great force: 千万要小心 (you absolutely must be careful), 千万别忘了 (whatever you do, don't forget).
铅笔	qiān bǐ	pencil — 铅 qiān (lead) + 笔 bǐ. The everyday pencil, named for the old idea of a "lead" pencil even though the core is graphite. One of the first writing tools a child learns to name.
签字	qiān zì	to sign
前辈	qián bèi	predecessor; senior; elder in one's field — 前 qián (before; preceding) + 辈 bèi (generation; people of the same era). Those of earlier generations who walked the path before you in your field, institution, or family. A term of respect: addressing someone as 前辈 acknowledges their experience and positions you as the newer arrival.
前朝	qián cháo	former dynasty; previous ruling house — 前 qián (former; preceding) + 朝 cháo (dynasty; court; morning). The dynasty that came before the current one , a term of historical reference used constantly in Chinese historical writing, since each dynasty defined itself partly in relation to what it replaced.
前方	qián fāng	ahead; the forward direction; the front (military) — 前 qián (front) + 方 fāng (direction; area; square). A more formal and often grander term than 前面 , used in military contexts, official broadcasts, and literary or elevated speech. 前方记者 (correspondent at the front) is a journalism term.
前后	qián hòu	front-back; before and after
前进	qián jìn	to advance; to go forward; to march ahead — 前 qián (front; forward) + 进 jìn (to advance). To move ahead in space or in cause: 向前进 "advance forward," 勇往直前 the spirit of pressing on. Its opposite is 后退 hòutuì, to fall back.
前面	qián miàn	in front; ahead; the front side — 前 qián (front) + 面 miàn (face; surface; side). The most common everyday expression for spatial "in front." Works for physical space (前面有个红绿灯 , there is a traffic light ahead) and for sequential position (前面的章节 , the preceding chapter).
前排	qián pái	front row — 前 qián (front) + 排 pái (row; line; rank). The front row of a theater, cinema, classroom, or any seated arrangement. Also used figuratively for first-rank prominence: 前排位置 (front-row position) implies visibility and status in any field.
前任	qián rèn	former occupant of a role; the "ex" (ex-partner, ex-boss) — 前 qián (former; preceding) + 任 rèn (appointment; term of office; to hold a post). The person who formerly held a given role or position.
前世	qián shì	a former life
前世今生	qián shì jīn shēng	past life and present life; across lifetimes — 前世 qiánshì (previous lifetime; past existence) + 今生 jīnshēng (this present life). A phrase that spans the axis of rebirth, linking the karmic conditions of a previous life to the circumstances of the current one.
前天	qián tiān	the day before yesterday — 前 qián (front; before) + 天 tiān (day; sky). The day that stands two steps "in front of" today.
前途	qián tú	future prospects; "front road"
前者	qián zhě	the former
钱包	qián bāo	wallet; purse — 钱 qián + 包 bāo (bag; to wrap). The wallet, literally the bag for money. In the smartphone era, 钱包 also refers to mobile payment wallets: 电子钱包 diànzǐ qiánbāo = digital wallet. 钱包里没钱 = the wallet is empty (a relatable condition).
钱给人骗了	qián gěi rén piàn le	the money was scammed (colloquial 给 passive) — 给 gěi as passive marker: Subject + 给 + Agent + Verb + Result. 给 in this passive function is particularly common in certain regional varieties of Mandarin. The adversarial connotation is strong , money being deceived out of someone is a very 被-appropriate scenario.
乾坤大挪移	qián kūn dà nuó yí	"the great cosmic shift" — a dramatic all-encompassing maneuver; a total reconfiguration — 挪移 nuó yí: to move; to shift; to relocate. 乾坤大挪移 names a fictional martial-arts technique in Jin Yong's (金庸) novel "The Smiling Proud Wanderer" (笑傲江湖) and appears in other wuxia fiction as the name for a supreme technique that redirects any force at will.
腔调	qiāng diào	accent; intonation; tone of speech — 腔 qiāng (cavity, the way speech resonates) + 调 diào (pitch, manner). The accent and intonation of a person's speech, often the regional or affected way they talk. 南方腔调 (a southern accent), 装腔作势 (put on airs). The sound that marks where a voice comes from.
强调	qiáng diào	to emphasize
墙脚	qiáng jiǎo	the foot of a wall; (figurative) one's foundation, one's base of support — 墙 qiáng (wall) + 脚. The base of a wall. The figurative idiom 挖墙脚 wā qiángjiǎo "to dig at the foot of the wall" means to undermine someone , poach their staff, steal their partner, erode their support , by attacking the foundation rather than confronting the wall directly.
抢救	qiǎng jiù	to rescue (emergency)
巧合	qiǎo hé	coincidence
亲近	qīn jìn	close and dear; intimate; to feel close to — 亲 qīn (family; intimate; close , the same phonetic component that appears in 新 as structural filler, but here fully semantic: kin, dear ones) + 近 (near). Closeness that is also warmth , proximity that has become affection.
亲朋	qīn péng	kin and friends: one's close circle — 亲 qīn (kin, relatives) + 朋 péng (friends). Relatives and friends taken together, the whole circle of those close to you. Most often heard in the four-character 亲朋好友, the standard phrase for everyone you would invite to a wedding or a feast.
亲情	qīn qíng	family affection; the bond of kinship — 亲 qīn (kin; close) + 情 qíng (feeling). The affection that runs between family members, the love of parent and child or among siblings. It completes the trio with 爱情 (love) and 友情 (friendship).
亲人	qīn rén	loved ones; dear family
钦天监	qīn tiān jiàn	Imperial Observatory / Bureau of Astronomy — Imperial Observatory / Bureau of Astronomy: the government department responsible for astronomical observation, calendar production, and astrological consultation in imperial China.
秦朝	qín cháo	the Qin dynasty
琴棋书画	qín qí shū huà	the four scholarly arts — qin, chess, calligraphy, painting — The canonical curriculum of the 文人 wénrén (literati) tradition. 琴 qín (guqin), 棋 qí (weiqi / go), 书 shū (calligraphy), 画 huà (painting). Proficiency in all four was the mark of an educated person.
青菜	qīng cài	green vegetables; leafy greens — 青 qīng (green) + 菜 cài (vegetable). A general word for leafy green vegetables, and in the south the name of a specific small green cabbage. 一盘青菜 "a plate of greens."
青春	qīng chūn	youth; the prime of life — 青 (qīng, green/blue, the color of new growth) + 春 (spring). "Green spring," the years of youth at their freshest. Used for the whole season of being young, often with a note of how briefly it lasts.
轻慢	qīng màn	to treat lightly; to show disrespect through dismissiveness — 轻 qīng (light, slight, to make little of) + 慢 màn (dismissive). To treat someone or something as if it barely deserves attention. More literary than 怠慢 or 傲慢. Often appears in classical texts and formal written criticism.
轻声	qīng shēng	neutral tone
轻信	qīng xìn	to believe too easily; credulity
倾听	qīng tīng	to listen attentively; to lean in and hear — 倾 qīng (to lean; to incline; to pour out) + 听 (to listen). Listening with the body inclined toward the speaker , attentive, empathetic, fully directed.
倾向	qīng xiàng	tendency; inclination; to lean toward — 倾 qīng (to lean; to tilt) + 向 xiàng (toward). The way a person or thing leans, a tendency or bias: 政治倾向 "political leanings." As a verb, to be inclined toward: 我倾向于同意 "I'm inclined to agree."
清白	qīng bái	innocence; moral integrity
清朝	qīng cháo	the Qing dynasty
清楚	qīng chu	clear, distinct — 清 (clear water) + 楚 (distinct). The clarity of things and statements: 说清楚 (say it clearly), 看清楚 (see it distinctly). Pairs with 明白 across the divide of world and mind: the map is 清楚, the reader is 明白.
清淡	qīng dàn	Clear and light , the flavor aesthetic of coastal and delta cuisines, particularly Cantonese. Emphasizes the natural flavors of fresh, high-quality ingredients with minimal masking by heavy seasoning. The direct expression of a geography where fresh seafood and produce are excellent and abundant.
清点	qīng diǎn	to check the count: to take stock
清洁	qīng jié	clean: cleanliness
清静	qīng jìng	quiet, still
清理	qīng lǐ	to clean up: to sort out
清凉	qīng liáng	cool, refreshing
清明	qīng míng	Clear and Bright — Clear and Bright: the solar term around April 4–6, one of the few solar terms that is also a public holiday in China (and Taiwan, Hong Kong). The Tomb-Sweeping Festival (清明节 Qīngmíngjié) falls on or near this term: families visit ancestral graves, sweep them, leave offerings, and burn paper goods.
清明节	Qīng míng jié	Tomb-Sweeping Festival
清明节扫墓	Qīng míng Jié Sǎo mù	Qingming — Tomb Sweeping — 清明节 (Clear and Bright Festival), falling around April 4–6 of the solar calendar, is the annual day of tomb sweeping (扫墓 sǎomù). Families travel to ancestral graves, clear away weeds, pour libations, burn paper offerings, and share a meal at the grave site.
清水	qīng shuǐ	clear water: plain water
清汤	qīng tāng	clear soup; clarified stock
清晰	qīng xī	clear and sharp: well-defined
清新	qīng xīn	fresh: clean and new
清真饮食	qīng zhēn yǐn shí	halal food — the most visible face of Hui culture — 清真 cuisine is a distinct tradition within Chinese cooking, developed by Hui communities over centuries. Core prohibitions: no pork (猪肉 zhūròu), no blood, no alcohol (in strictly observant contexts), and meat must be slaughtered according to Islamic rite (念清真 niàn qīngzhēn).
清蒸鱼	qīng zhēng yú	Steamed Fish
情报	qíng bào	intelligence, information
情感	qíng gǎn	emotion (literary)
情歌	qíng gē	love song — 情 (feeling, romance) plus 歌 (song). A love song, one of the most productive 歌 compounds in popular music.
情况	qíng kuàng	situation; circumstances; condition — 情 qíng (circumstance) + 况 kuàng (condition). The standard word for a situation or set of circumstances: 了解情况 "to understand the situation," 紧急情况 "an emergency."
情人	qíng rén	lover; sweetheart
情形	qíng xíng	situation; circumstances; state of affairs — 情 qíng (circumstance; feeling) + 形 xíng. The plain, everyday word for a situation or set of circumstances. 实际情形 = the actual situation; 这种情形 = this kind of case. Close to 情况 qíngkuàng and often interchangeable, with 情形 leaning slightly more descriptive.
情绪	qíng xù	emotion; emotional state; mood (often the volatile side) — 情 qíng (feeling) + 绪 xù (threads; strands). The tangled threads of feeling, an emotional state that can run high or low: 控制情绪 "to control one's emotions," 闹情绪 "to be in a mood; to sulk."
晴天 · 雨天 · 阴天	qíng tiān yǔ tiān yīn tiān	sunny day · rainy day · overcast day — 天 tiān as suffix: "day of [weather type]." The pattern (weather adjective + 天) is one of the most productive in spoken Chinese. 晴 qíng (clear); 雨 yǔ (rain); 阴 yīn (overcast, shadow-side). Also: 雪天 xuětiān (snowy day), 风天 fēngtiān (windy day), 大热天 dà rètiān (scorching hot day).
请多关照	qǐng duō guān zhào	please look after us; I look forward to working with you — The standard closing line of a first introduction, asking the other side's goodwill for the relationship ahead. 初次见面，请多关照 ("meeting for the first time, please look after me") is the full formula. 请多指教 asks for guidance and is slightly humbler.
请教	qǐng jiào	to consult; to ask for advice (politely) — 请 qǐng (to request) + 教 jiào (instruction). To respectfully ask someone to teach you, the polite way to seek advice from a senior or an expert: 向您请教 "may I ask your guidance." Here 教 returns to the fourth tone.
请客吃饭	qǐng kè chī fàn	hosting a meal — baijiu is the host's primary tool
请神明	qǐng shén míng	to invite a deity's presence; to install a divine figure ritually — 请 qǐng (to invite; to request). The ritual act of inviting a deity to be present , either into a statue during a consecration ceremony, into a temporary vessel at a festival, or into a new altar. The statue itself is 神像 shénxiàng; the consecration that animates it with divine presence is the 请神明.
请问	qǐng wèn	may I ask; excuse me (before a question) — 请 qǐng (please; to request) + 问 wèn (to ask). The polite opener for putting a question to a stranger, much like English "excuse me, may I ask." One of the first phrases a learner needs for asking directions.
穷则变，变则通，通则久	qióng zé biàn , biàn zé tōng , tōng zé jiǔ	when exhausted, change; when changed, break through; when through, endure — From the 系辞下传 (Commentary on the Attached Phrases, Part II), one of the Ten Wings. 穷 qióng here means not poverty but exhaustion: having reached a dead end, used up all options, hit the wall. 变 biàn: transform, change the approach. 通 tōng: break through, find passage, flow freely again.
秋千	qiū qiān	a swing (the playground kind) — 秋 qiū + 千 qiān, written 秋千 or 鞦韆. Here 千 is purely phonetic, lending its sound to a word for a swing that has nothing to do with the number. 荡秋千 dàng qiūqiān is to swing on a swing.
秋天	qiū tiān	autumn
求救	qiú jiù	to call for help
求雨	qiú yǔ	rain calling — interceding with sky spirits — Rain-calling (求雨 qiú yǔ) bridges shamanic and folk-religion traditions: the shaman performs extended trance-dancing, drumming, and offering to the spirits of rain and sky (天神 tiānshén), petitioning them to release precipitation.
球队	qiú duì	sports team (ball game) — 球 (ball) + 队 (team). Any club built around a ball sport: football, basketball, volleyball. Swap the first character for the sport's tool.
趋向	qū xiàng	tendency; trend
趋向补语	qū xiàng bǔ yǔ	directional complement
取代	qǔ dài	to supersede; to replace; to displace — 取 qǔ (to take) + 代 dài (the place of). To take over another's place and push it out entirely: 新技术取代了旧技术 "the new technology superseded the old." Stronger and more decisive than 代替, with a sense that the old thing is now gone.
取决于	qǔ ju é yú	to depend on — The follow-up question to every 应该 and 尽量: find the condition behind the hedge. Once the condition is named, it can be negotiated.
取名	qǔ míng	to name; to give a name — 取 qǔ (to take; to select; to acquire) + 名 míng (name). The act of choosing a name , for a child, a product, a shop, a poem.
去吧	qù ba	go ahead; you may go; off you go — 去 qù (to go; to depart) + 吧 ba (softening particle, suggestion or permission). A gentle dismissal or permission to leave. In a parent-child conversation: 去吧，好好玩 (Go on , have fun). In a formal context: 你去吧，我在这等 (Go ahead , I'll wait here).
去北京的火车	qù Běi jīng de huǒ chē	the train to Beijing — clause + 的 + noun — 的 can follow entire clauses or verb phrases to mark modification of the following noun. This is Chinese's primary relative clause mechanism , there are no separate relative pronouns. The entire clause precedes 的 which directly precedes the noun being modified.
去除	qù chú	to remove; to eliminate; to get rid of — 去 qù (to send away; to remove) + 除 chú (to eliminate; to remove; to divide out). To cause something to go away , to strip out an unwanted element. Used in formal and technical contexts: 去除污染 (remove contamination), 去除杂质 (remove impurities), 去除顾虑 (dispel concerns).
去掉	qù diào	to get rid of; to remove; to drop (something) — 去 qù (to cause to go) + 掉 diào (resultative complement: dropped away; gone). A colloquial and direct expression for removal. 掉 as a complement emphasizes that the thing has been fully removed and is gone. More informal than 去除; appropriate for everyday speech. 把它去掉！= Get rid of it!
去年	qùn ián	last year — 去 qù (to have gone; to have departed) + 年 nián (year). The year that has departed , last year. A vivid temporal use: the year that went away. Contrast: 来年 láinián (the year that is coming , next year; somewhat literary) and 今年 jīnnián (this year).
去声	qù shēng	the departing tone; tone 4
去世	qù shì	to pass away; to die (respectful) — 去 qù (to depart; to leave) + 世 shì (the world; this age; this life). To depart from the world , the standard respectful expression for the death of an adult. Not used for children or animals, and not used for enemies or condemned criminals (for those, more neutral or harsher terms apply).
全 · 整	quán zhěng	whole vs. entire-and-unbroken — 全 fuses directly onto nouns to mean "the whole": 全家 (the whole family), 全国 (the whole country), 全世界 (the whole world). 整 zhěng insists the unit is complete and uncut: 整个 (the entire), 整天 (all day long), 整整三年 (three full years).
全部	quán bù	all; the whole; entire — 全 quán (whole) + 部 bù (part; section). The complete set of parts, every one included: 全部作品 "the complete works," 全部完成 "all finished." It points at the totality of a definite group of things.
全都	quán dōu	all; every one; without exception — 全 quán (entirely) + 都 dōu (all). A reinforced "all," placed before the verb to stress that the whole group is included: 答案全都对 "every answer is right." The two totality words stack for emphasis.
全国	quáng uó	the whole country; nationwide — 全 quán (whole) + 国 guó (country). The entire nation as one extent: 全国人民 "the whole nation's people," 全国各地 "all parts of the country." A model for 全 + place: 全省 the whole province, 全市 the whole city.
全家	quán jiā	the whole family; the entire household — 全 quán (whole) + 家 jiā (family; home). The family taken as a complete unit: 全家福 "a whole-family photo," 全家团圆 "the whole family reunited." A warm, everyday use of the whole sense.
全靠	quán kào	to rely entirely on; to owe it all to — 全 quán (entirely) + 靠 kào (to lean on; to depend). To depend wholly on one person or thing, with nothing else to fall back on: 全靠大家的努力 "thanks entirely to everyone's effort."
全面	quán miàn	comprehensive; all-sided
全名	quán míng	Full name , surname + given name together — Full name , surname + given name together. 请问您贵姓？(qǐngwèn nín guì xìng?) is the polite form of "May I ask your surname?" — literally "May I ask your honorable surname?"
全球化	quán qiú huà	globalization — the context and consequence
全体	quán tǐ	all (of a group of people); the entire body — 全 quán (whole) + 体 tǐ (body). The entire body of people taken together, used of members, staff, or citizens: 全体学生 "all the students," 全体起立 "everybody stand up." Where 全部 counts things, 全体 gathers people.
全新	quán xīn	brand new
权力	quán lì	authority; power
泉眼	quán yǎn	the eye of a spring; the place where spring water emerges — 泉 quán (spring) + 眼. The mouth of a natural spring , the small opening from which water bubbles up. Common in classical Chinese poetry and travel writing.
缺德	qu ē dé	unscrupulous; lacking moral decency; rotten (colloquial) — 缺 quē (to lack) + 德. To be missing virtue. The everyday Chinese accusation for someone whose conduct is not just unkind but morally wrong in a low way , petty cruelty, dishonesty for its own sake, malicious mischief. 太缺德了！ "That's so unscrupulous!" is one of the standard everyday condemnations.
缺点	qu ē diǎn	shortcoming
确定	qu è dìng	to confirm; to be sure; certain — 确 què (sure; firm) + 定 dìng (to settle). To pin a thing down as fixed and beyond doubt, or to be sure of it oneself. 我不确定 "I'm not sure," 确定时间 "to fix the time."
确认	qu èr èn	to confirm
确认样	qu èr èn yàng	approval sample — The sample the buyer has approved, usually signed and dated. Everything after it is measured against it, so record exactly which version you approved and what you asked to change.
确认一下	qu èr èn yí xià	let me confirm — 确认 (quèrèn) is the verb of the whole relationship: samples are confirmed, drawings are confirmed, orders are confirmed. 我确认一下 before restating a point; 您确认一下 when handing the other side something to check.
确实	qu è shí	indeed; truly
群体	qún tǐ	group; collective
然而	rán ér	"However" (formal) — "However" (formal). The more literary cousin of 不过, common in written and formal spoken contexts. In casual conversation it can sound bookish; in lectures, presentations, and considered discussions it fits naturally.
让价	ràng jià	to concede on price — 让 is "to yield." 让利 (rànglì) is giving up margin; 降价 (jiàngjià) is simply lowering the price, 涨价 (zhǎngjià) raising it, 还价 (huánjià) making a counteroffer. 底价 (dǐjià) is the floor price a side will not go below.
让我想想	ràng wǒ xiǎng xiang	"Let me think — "Let me think." Direct, slightly more formal than 那个. Appropriate when a question deserves a real answer and you want the listener to wait while you produce one. The reduplicated 想想 softens it, suggesting brief consideration rather than a long pause.
热爱	rè ài	to love ardently
热点	rè diǎn	hot spot; trending topic
热敷	rè fū	hot compress — 热 (hot) plus 敷 (fū, to apply to the skin): to apply heat, a hot compress. The home remedy for a stiff neck or a sore back, the warm counterpart to 冷敷 (lěngfū), a cold compress.
热烈	rè liè	fervent, intense
热门	rè mén	popular, in demand — 热 (hot) plus 门 (mén, gate, field): a hot gateway, hence a popular field, trending topic, or in-demand option. The opposite is 冷门 (lěngmén), a cold and obscure one.
热闹	rèn ao	lively, bustling — 热 (hot) plus 闹 (nào, noisy, to make a din): the heat of a busy, crowded, festive scene. Note the neutral tone on 闹 in this word. A market, a holiday street, a full restaurant are all 热闹.
热情	rè qíng	enthusiasm; warmth; warmly hospitable — 热 rè (hot) + 情 qíng (feeling). Warm feeling, used both as a noun (enthusiasm, passion) and as an adjective for a warm, welcoming person: 他很热情 "he is very warm and friendly."
热水	rè shuǐ	hot water — 热 (hot) plus 水 (shuǐ, water). The everyday word for hot water, the staple drink offered to a guest and the cure a Chinese parent prescribes for almost anything.
热心	rè xīn	warm-hearted
人才	rén cái	a talented person; talent; capable people — 人 rén (person) + 才 cái (talent). A person of real ability, and by extension the pool of skilled people an organization or country can draw on: 培养人才 "to cultivate talent," 人才市场 "the job market for skilled workers."
人称	rén chēng	grammatical person
人称代词	rén chēng dài cí	personal pronoun
人道	rén dào	the human realm; the human path of rebirth — The human realm is considered the most favorable position for Buddhist practice precisely because of its mixture of suffering and capacity. Humans experience enough pain and impermanence to feel the urgency of liberation, while retaining enough cognitive clarity and agency to pursue the path.
人工	réng ōng	artificial; manual labor
人工智能	réng ōng zhìn éng	artificial intelligence; AI — 人工 réngōng (man-made; artificial , 人 person + 工 work/craft) + 智能 zhìnéng (intelligent capability , 智 wisdom/intelligence + 能 capability/ability). Abbreviated 人工智能 or simply AI in technical contexts; 智能 alone is used as an adjective: 智能手机 zhìnéng shǒujī (smartphone), 智能家居 zhìnéng jiājū (smart home).
人海	rén hǎi	a sea of people; a vast crowd — 人 rén (person) + 海 hǎi (sea). A crowd so large it reads as an ocean of heads. Famous in the phrase 茫茫人海 "the boundless sea of humanity," the throng in which two people might never meet.
人际关系	rén jì guān xi	interpersonal relationships; social connections — 人际 rén jì = between people (人 person + 际 boundary, junction). 人际关系 is the standard term for the full web of interpersonal relationships in Chinese social and professional life. Appears constantly in business advice, psychology, and self-help contexts.
人家	rén jia	other people; someone's home; (colloquial) I/me — 人 rén (person) + 家 jiā (home; family). This single compound has three distinct uses in modern Mandarin: (1) other people in general; (2) someone's specific household; (3) an informal first-person pronoun used primarily by women, expressing mild protest or vulnerability.
人间佛教	rén jiān fó jiào	humanistic Buddhism; Buddhism for the human world — The 20th-century reformist movement, associated above all with Master Taixu (太虚, 1890–1947), that repositioned Buddhist practice away from funeral rites and other-worldly concerns toward engagement with society, education, and the relief of present suffering.
人间天堂	rén jiān tiān táng	paradise on earth; heaven in the human world — 天堂 (tiāntáng) = paradise; heaven. 人间天堂 collapses the cosmological distance between 人间 and 天界: a place so beautiful it brings the celestial into the human world.
人间烟火	rén jiān yān huǒ	the smoke and fire of human life; the warmth of ordinary domestic existence — 烟火 (yānhuǒ) = smoke and fire , specifically the smoke of cooking fires and the warmth of a hearth. 人间烟火 refers to the sights, smells, and sounds of ordinary human life: street food stalls, the smell of garlic in a wok, a neighborhood at dusk.
人间蒸发	rén jiān zhēng fā	"to evaporate from the human world" — to vanish; to go completely off the grid — 蒸发 (zhēngfā) = to evaporate; to vaporize. A colorful colloquial expression for someone who has completely disappeared from contact , not answering calls, not posting online, impossible to locate. The humor is cosmological: they have not merely left town, they have vacated 人间 entirely.
人口	rén kǒu	population — lit. "people-mouths" — 人 rén (person) + 口 kǒu (mouth). Population , the number of mouths to feed, the count of human presences. 中国人口约14亿 "China's population is approximately 1.4 billion." 人口众多 rénkǒu zhòngduō = "large population" (a standard description of China).
人类	rén lèi	humanity; humankind; the human species — 人 rén + 类 lèi (species; category; kind). Refers to humanity as a biological and civilizational category, the human species in its entirety across all time. Used in philosophical, scientific, and grand-historical registers. Much larger in scope than 人们, and without political coloring.
人脉	rén mài	network; professional connections (lit. "person-veins") — 人 rén + 脉 mài (vein; pulse; artery, the channels through which blood flows). Your social and professional network, imagined as a circulatory system. 脉 is the same character used in 经脉 jīngmài (meridians) in TCM.
人们	rén men	people (indefinite plural) — 人 rén + 们 men (plural suffix for animate nouns). A general, indefinite plural: "people" in the broad social sense, as in "one finds that people…" or "people say…" 们 cannot be combined with numbers; you cannot say ＊三人们. This plural is for social generality, not counting.
人民	rén mín	the people (political collective) — 人 rén + 民 mín (common people; subjects; citizens). A politically weighted term. In the PRC context, it carries strong ideological resonance: the people as a collective subject and political actor, not merely a demographic count. Appears in major institutional names and slogans.
人民币	rén mín bì	renminbi, RMB
人品	rén pǐn	moral character; the quality of a person — 人 rén + 品 pǐn (quality; grade; character, three 口 mouths stacked, suggesting the spoken judgments of a community). The overall moral quality of a person as assessed by those around them: moral trustworthiness and reliability in relationships, not talent or intelligence.
人情	rén qíng	human feeling; social obligation; the gift economy of favors — Human feeling, social obligation , the accumulated weight of favors, gifts, and consideration exchanged between people. To "owe someone rénqíng" is to be in their social debt. Gift-giving is one of the primary means of building and repaying 人情. The concept is inseparable from 关系.
人群	rén qún	crowd
人世	rén shì	the human world
人物	rén wù	figure; personage; character (in a story) — 人 rén (person) + 物 wù (thing). A notable person, a "somebody," and also a character in a novel, film, or play: 历史人物 "a historical figure," 主要人物 "the main character."
