音乐家	yīn yu è jiā	musician (mastery level); composer — 音乐 yīnyuè (music) + 家 jiā. Implies serious, dedicated musical mastery: a composer, a concert performer, a conductor rather than a casual musician. Distinguished from 歌手 gēshǒu (singer/pop artist) by the 家 suffix, which implies depth, discipline, and classical standing.
音量	yīn liàng	volume; sound level
音信	yīn xìn	news; word; tidings (of a person) — 音 yīn (sound; word) + 信 xìn (message; letter). News or word of someone far away. Most common in the negative: 没有音信 "no word at all," and the idiom 杳无音信, vanished without a trace.
音韵	yīn yùn	Guanyin rhyme — Tieguanyin's signature quality
银河	yín hé	the Milky Way — 银 (yín, silver) + 河 (river). A silver river across the night sky. Chinese named the galaxy as a river of stars long before it was a galaxy, and the metaphor stuck.
银行	yín háng	bank — 银 yín (silver) + 行 háng. The silver-row , originally a row of money-changers along a market street, then by extension the modern banking institution. The single most-tested 行-háng word: students who default to xíng on every 行 will read this wrong forever.
引进	yǐn jìn	to introduce; to bring in (technology, talent, methods) — 引 yǐn (to draw; to lead) + 进 jìn (to take in). To bring something in from outside, typically from abroad: 引进技术 "introduce technology," 引进人才 "bring in talent."
饮茶	yǐn chá	yum cha; going for dim sum; drinking tea
饮食文化	yǐn shí wén huà	food culture; culinary civilization — 饮食 yǐnshí (food and drink, diet) + 文化 (culture). Chinese food culture is one of the most discussed topics in 文化 discourse , not just cuisine but the entire social system of eating: banquet etiquette, regional identity, seasonal eating, the pairing of food with medicine and philosophy.
窨花	xùn huā	scenting — the process of infusing tea with flower fragrance
应当	yīng dāng	ought to; should; be obliged to — 应 yīng (should) + 当 dāng (be fitting). A modal of obligation, near-identical in meaning to 应该 yīnggāi but slightly more formal, so it shows up often in rules, contracts, and writing.
应付	yìng fu	to cope with; to handle; to deal with — 应 yìng (to meet) + 付 fù (to hand over, to deal out). To handle a task or person, often a difficult one. Can carry a tinge of just getting through it: 应付考试 (manage to get through the exam), 应付了事 (do something perfunctorily just to be done with it).
应该是	yīng gāi shì	should be; probably is
应聘	yìng pìn	to apply for a job
应用	yìng yòng	to apply; application
英明	yīng míng	brilliant; enlightened (of a leader) — 英 yīng (outstanding; heroic; talent that flowers) + 明 míng (luminous). The compound used to praise rulers, commanders, and decision-makers of exceptional vision. 英明的领导 "an enlightened leader."
英武	yīng wǔ	valiant and impressive; heroic in bearing — 英 yīng (heroic, outstanding) + 武 wǔ (martial). Of a person, valiant and impressive in look and manner, the brave, spirited bearing of a hero or a fine soldier: 英武不凡 "valiant and out of the ordinary." A literary, admiring word, often used of a young officer or commander.
迎接	yíng jiē	to welcome, to go out to meet — 迎 (yíng, to go toward) + 接 (to receive). You walk out to meet an arrival and bring them in. Often warm or ceremonial: greeting guests, soldiers, the new year.
影子	yǐng zi	shadow
硬件	yìng jiàn	hardware
拥有	yōng yǒu	to own; to cherish; to hold close — 拥 yōng (to embrace; to hold close; to crowd together) + 有. More emotionally warm than 所有 or 具有. Suggests not just legal or abstract possession but holding something dear. Used for things of personal value: relationships, opportunities, qualities of character, cherished experiences.
永乐帝	Yǒng lè Dì	third Ming emperor, builder of Beijing
永明延寿	Yǒng míng Yán shòu	Yongming Yanshou (904–975 CE) — Song dynasty Chan-Pure Land synthesis — The sixth patriarch of Pure Land and a major Chan master simultaneously, Yanshou embodied the Chinese Buddhist principle that the two traditions are not opposed but complementary.
用法	yòng fǎ	usage; how something is used — 用 yòng (to use) + 法 fǎ (way). The way a thing is properly used, especially a word or a tool: 这个词的用法 "the usage of this word." Built on the same "way of doing" sense as 方法.
用功	yòng ōng	to study hard; to work diligently; to apply oneself — 用 yòng (to use; to deploy) + 功 gōng (effort; merit; achievement). To deploy effort , the literal meaning maps exactly onto the English "to apply oneself." Used particularly of students and academic work, but extends to any disciplined sustained effort.
用力	yòng lì	to exert force; to use one's strength; hard (of physical effort) — 用 yòng (to use) + 力 lì (force). To put physical force into an action: 用力推 "push hard," 用力拉 "pull with all your strength." Describes how an action is done, with muscle behind it.
用途	yòng tú	use; purpose; application; intended function — 用 yòng (use; function) + 途 tú (route; destination; intended course). The destination of deployment: what something is for, where its use is headed. 用途 answers the question "what is this for?" and tends to describe a range of applications rather than a single act of using.
用心	yòng xīn	attentively; with care
优点	yōu diǎn	strong point; merit; advantage — 优 yōu (excellent) + 点 diǎn (point). A good point, a strength. Its exact opposite is 缺点 quēdiǎn, a shortcoming. Together they are the standard pair for weighing a person, plan, or product.
优美	yōu měi	graceful; elegant
优质产品	yōu zhì chǎn pǐn	high-quality product; premium product — 优质 yōuzhì (excellent quality , 优 excellent + 质 substance/quality) is the premium tier modifier. 打造优质产品 (to build premium products) is a common mission statement. Contrasts with 劣质产品 (lièzhì chǎnpǐn, inferior-quality products) , counterfeit or substandard goods.
尤其	yóu qí	especially; in particular; above all — 尤 yóu (outstanding; especially) + 其 qí (that; those). "Especially that" , used to single out one item from a broader set as particularly true or notable. Appears before verbs, adjectives, or noun phrases. Roughly equivalent to "particularly" or "above all."
由于	yóu yú	due to; owing to; because of — 由 yóu (from) + 于 yú (at; in). A formal, written near-synonym of 因为, marking the cause at the front of a sentence: 由于天气原因，航班取消了 "owing to the weather, the flight was cancelled." It pairs with 因此 rather than 所以.
犹如	yóu rú	just as; like
邮件	yóu jiàn	mail; email; a postal item — 邮 yóu (post; mail) + 件 jiàn (a piece). Originally any item sent through the post. In everyday modern use it most often means email: 电子邮件 diànzǐ yóujiàn (electronic mail) is regularly shortened to 邮件. To send one is 发邮件 fā yóujiàn.
邮票	yóu piào	postage stamp: a stamp for mailing letters — 邮 yóu (post; mail) + 票 piào (slip). A postage stamp: a tiny printed slip stuck to an envelope that stands for prepaid postage. It is 票 in miniature, a small piece of paper carrying a fixed value, and a favorite object of collectors (集邮 jíyóu, stamp collecting).
油画	yóu huà	oil painting — 油 yóu (oil) + 画 huà (painting). The Western art of painting in oils, named for its medium. Its native counterpart is 国画 guóhuà, named for its nation rather than its material.
游船	yóu chuán	pleasure boat, cruise boat
友好	yǒu hǎo	friendly; amicable
友情	yǒu qíng	friendship; the feeling between friends — 友 yǒu (friend) + 情 qíng (feeling). The bond of friendship. Close to 友谊 yǒuyì in meaning, but 友情 leans on the felt warmth, while 友谊 leans on the formal relationship.
有道理	yǒu dào lǐ	to make sense; to be reasonable; that's a fair point — 有 yǒu (to have; there is) + 道理 dàolǐ (reason; logic). "To have reason," to possess the quality of making sense. One of the most common spoken responses to an argument you find convincing, used the way "fair point," "that makes sense," and "good point" function in English.
有的	yǒu de	some (of a set); certain ones — 有 + 的 (nominalizing particle). Functions as an indefinite partitive , "some of [a set already mentioned or implied]." The pattern 有的…有的… (some…others…) distributes a set into contrasting subgroups and is one of the most natural ways to express "some people…some people…" in Chinese.
有点	yǒu diǎn	a bit; slightly (pre-verbal, negative or complaint coloring) — 有 + 点 diǎn (a dot; a small amount). Always appears before verbs and adjectives as a pre-modifier. The key nuance: 有点 carries a slightly negative or complaint-inflected tone. You use it for problems, inconveniences, or things that fall short.
有点儿	yǒu diǎn r	a bit; somewhat (often "a bit too…") — Placed before an adjective (or a feeling-verb) to say something is "a bit / somewhat" that way, usually with a tinge of complaint or an unwanted state. 有点儿 + 累 / 冷 / 贵 / 难 = a bit tired / cold / expensive / hard. It describes a current condition the speaker finds slightly undesirable.
有关	yǒu guān	related, relevant; concerned (with)
有关系	yǒu guān xi	to be related; to matter; to have a bearing on — 有关系 means there is a connection, relevance, or effect between two things. 这跟我有关系吗？= "Does this concern me / affect me?" Used to establish relevance, causation, or connection. Contrast with 有关 yǒuguān (related to; concerning , slightly more formal, often in 有关部门, "relevant departments").
有害	yǒu hài	harmful, noxious — 有 (to have) + 害 (harm): possessing the capacity to wound. Its antonym 无害 (wúhài) marks a thing as harmless. Frequent on labels and in science writing.
有空	yǒu kòng	to have free time
有空再联系	yǒu kòng zài lián xì	"Keep in touch when you have time — "Keep in touch when you have time." Slightly more open-ended than 改天再聊. Suggests that contact will resume when both schedules permit. Polite and standard.
有礼貌	yǒu lǐ mào	polite; well-mannered; courteous — 有 yǒu (to have) + 礼貌. The default form of approval for someone's social bearing. Applied across the age range , to children, colleagues, strangers, foreigners , and across formality levels. 这个孩子很有礼貌 ("this child is very polite") is a high compliment to the parents as much as to the child.
有没有	yǒu méi yǒu	do you have? / is there? (A-not-A question) — The A-not-A question form of 有. Used both for possession ("do you have X?") and for existence ("is there X?"). In rapid speech, 有没有 is often compressed or the object follows immediately: 有没有时间？ Also used as a sentence-final tag: 你来过北京，有没有？ — "You've been to Beijing, haven't you?"
有面子	yǒu miàn zi	to have face; to be prestigious; to feel honored — To possess and display face , to be in a position of recognized prestige or to feel that your standing has been acknowledged or elevated. Certain possessions, positions, and associations give face: luxury goods, titles, famous friends, prestigious education.
有名	yǒu míng	famous; well-known — 有 yǒu (to have; to possess) + 名 míng (name; fame). To have a name that people know , the most common adjective for "famous" in spoken Mandarin. Neutral in register, works for people, places, dishes, and brands alike.
有钱	yǒu qián	to have money, rich
有人	yǒu rén	there is someone; someone (existential + indefinite reference) — 有 in the existential construction introduces a person into the discourse. 有人 can function as the subject of a following verb: 有人说… (Someone said…; There are people who say…). This is a common way to introduce an indefinite agent , "some people say," "someone thinks," "there are those who believe."
有时	yǒu shí	sometimes; at times — 有 + 时 shí (time). One of the most basic time adverbs: "at some times; sometimes." Often appears in the paired pattern 有时…有时… (sometimes…sometimes…) to describe alternating or variable states. 有时候 yǒu shíhou is the slightly more colloquial form (literally "at some time-instances").
有时候	yǒu shí hou	sometimes — "Sometimes," literally "there are times." Often shortened to 有时. The paired form 有时候…有时候… means "sometimes… and other times…," a neat way to describe alternating situations.
有事	yǒu shì	to be busy; to have something come up; to have a matter to attend to — 有 yǒu (have) + 事 shì. "Have a matter." Used to beg off (something has come up) or to flag that you need something from someone: 我有事找你 "I have something to discuss with you."
有所	yǒu suǒ	somewhat; to some extent; there is some degree of
有为	yǒu wéi	capable; purposeful; with ambition and scope to act; achieving — 有 yǒu (to have; to possess) + 为 wéi (action; doing; purposeful agency). The counterpart to 无为 , intentional, directed, deliberate action.
有问题	yǒu wèn tí	there's a problem; there's a question — The genuinely ambiguous phrase: it can mean "I have a question" or "there's a problem / something's wrong," and only context disambiguates. 有问题吗？after an explanation means "any questions?"; 这里有问题 about a machine means "there's a problem here."
有希望	yǒu xī wàng	to have hope; to be promising — "There is hope," used of a situation that may yet turn out well: 病人还有希望 ("the patient still has hope"). It can also mean "promising" of a person or prospect: 这孩子很有希望 ("this child is very promising"). The negative 没有希望 ("there's no hope") and the verb 失望 ("to be let down") sit on the other side.
有效期	yǒu xiào qī	validity period — How long a quote holds. Factories tie it to material prices, especially steel, and to the exchange rate (汇率 huìlǜ). A quote with no date can be reopened at any time.
有意思	yǒu yì si	interesting; fun; entertaining; appealing — Lit. "has meaning/appeal." The go-to word for "interesting" in casual spoken Chinese. Used for books, films, people, topics, situations , anything with engaging appeal.
有用	yǒu yòng	useful; of use
有余涅槃	yǒu yú niè pán	nirvana with remainder; liberation while still embodied — 有余 (with a remainder) + 涅槃. The state of an awakened person, an arhat or a buddha, who has extinguished the three fires but still carries a body whose karmic momentum continues. The Buddha after his awakening at Bodh Gayā lived for forty more years; that life was 有余涅槃.
有缘	yǒu yuán	to have a karmic connection; fated to meet — 有缘 means that a karmic connection exists between people , that the conditions for their meeting were in place.
又红又专	yòu hóng yòu zhuān	both red and expert; politically loyal and professionally capable — 又 yòu...又 yòu (both...and) framing 红 (red, politically reliable) and 专 zhuān (expert, specialized). A defining slogan of the Mao era: the ideal cadre or worker was supposed to be ideologically loyal and technically skilled at once.
又来了	yòu lái le	here we go again — Deployed at the first bars of a familiar tune: the uncle's stock speech, the app's renewal popup, the roommate's diet announcement. 你又来了 aims it at a person, affection and exasperation mixed to taste.
右边	yòu biān	the right side; on the right — 右 (right) + 边 (side; edge). The neutral everyday word for "the right side." 在右边 (on the right), 右边的窗户 (the window on the right). The paired form 左边 zuǒbiān (the left side) appears constantly alongside it.
右派	yòu pài	the right faction; right-wing — 右 (right) + 派 (faction, school, stream). Modern political term adopted from Western usage. In PRC political history, 右派 took on specific weight during the Anti-Rightist Campaign (反右运动 Fǎn Yòu Yùndòng, 1957–1959) launched after the Hundred Flowers Campaign.
右手	yòu shǒu	the right hand — 右 (right) + 手 (hand). The right hand , the dominant hand in the original character, the hand raised to the mouth. In Chinese calligraphy instruction, 右手执笔 (hold the brush with the right hand) was the standard prescription.
于是	yú shì	thereupon; as a result; and so — 于 yú (at; in; given) + 是 (this; the situation). Classical origin: "at this point; given this situation." A narrative conjunction that advances a story , signaling consequence or the next development in a sequence. Slightly formal register.
盂兰盆节	Yú lán pén Jié	Ghost Festival — the great Buddhist-folk religion synthesis — Held on the 15th day of the 7th lunar month, the midpoint of the "Ghost Month" 鬼月 during which the spirits of the dead are believed to return to the world of the living. Families set out food offerings, burn paper goods, and float river lanterns to guide the spirits.
娱乐	yú lè	entertainment; recreation; to amuse oneself — 娱 yú (to amuse) + 乐 lè (joy). Entertainment or recreation, both the activities and the having of fun: 娱乐活动 "recreational activities," 娱乐圈 "the entertainment world."
渔船	yú chuán	fishing boat — 渔 (to fish) + 船 (boat): a boat worked for the catch. 渔 carries the water radical 氵, marking the act of fishing, distinct from 鱼 the fish itself.
渔夫	yú fū	fisherman — 渔 yú (to fish) + 夫 fū (man). A man who makes his living by fishing. Like 农夫 it has a timeless, story-book ring, and it features in the famous proverb about the fisherman who profits while the snipe and the clam are locked in struggle.
渔民	yú mín	fishermen; Mazu's core devotees
愉快	yú kuài	pleasant; cheerful; agreeable — 愉 yú (pleased; at ease; the heart-radical with a sound component suggesting relaxed breathing) + 快 kuài (unobstructed joy). More refined and slightly more formal than 快乐. The word you reach for when describing an experience, a meeting, or an atmosphere as genuinely pleasant.
舆论	yú lùn	public opinion — 舆 yú (the common people; literally a carriage, by extension the public) + 论. The collective voice of the public on an issue: public opinion as a force. 舆论压力 yúlùn yālì "pressure of public opinion," 引导舆论 yǐndǎo yúlùn "to guide public opinion."
与其	yǔ qí	rather than; instead of — 与 yǔ (with; and; compare) + 其 qí (that). "Compared with that" , introduces the rejected alternative in a preference structure. Almost always paired with 不如 bùrú (not as good as; better to) or 宁可 nìngkě (would rather). The full construction: 与其 A, 不如 B , "rather than A, better to B."
与其等待，不如行动	yǔ qí děng dài , bù rú xíng dòng	rather than waiting, it's better to act — The simplest pattern: verb phrases on both sides. 与其 + action to reject, 不如 + action to recommend. The rhetorical punch: waiting is rejected as the inferior choice; action is endorsed.
羽化升天	yǔ huà shēng tiān	ascension to Heaven — her death and deification — In 987 CE, at age twenty-seven or twenty-eight, Lin Mo climbed Meizhou Island's highest point. Witnesses reported hearing celestial music (仙乐 xiānyuè) and seeing her surrounded by colored clouds as she ascended into the sky.
雨季	yǔ jì	rainy season
雨天	yǔ tiān	rainy day
语法	yǔ fǎ	grammar — 语 yǔ (language; speech) + 法 fǎ (rule; law). The "law of language," the system of rules by which a language is built. The same 法 of fixed standard, here governing how words combine.
语录	yǔ lù	recorded sayings of Chan masters
语气	yǔ qì	tone of voice; grammatical mood; modal register — 语 yǔ (language; speech) + 气 qì. The qi of language, how something is said rather than what. In grammatical analysis, 语气 = mood (indicative, imperative, interrogative).
语气词	yǔ qì cí	modal particle
语文	yǔ wén	language arts; Chinese (as a school subject) — 语 yǔ (language; speech) + 文 wén (writing; culture; literature). The Chinese school subject covering reading, writing, classical texts, and composition , the equivalent of "English" class in an English-speaking curriculum, but broader in scope because it encompasses classical Chinese literature along…
语言	yǔ yán	language (as a system) — 语 yǔ (language; speech; to tell) + 言 yán (speech; words). The word for language as a structured system , grammar, vocabulary, and everything that makes communication possible across a community. 语言 is used in academic, formal, and everyday contexts alike. 语言学 yǔyánxué = linguistics.
语义	yǔ yì	semantic meaning (linguistics)
语音	yǔ yīn	voice message — Factory staff often send long voice messages. 转文字 (zhuǎn wénzì) converts a voice message to text inside WeChat (press and hold the message), and the result is easy to paste into a translator. Asking for text is acceptable when phrased as your limitation.
玉皇大帝	Yù huáng Dà dì	the Jade Emperor — supreme deity of the folk pantheon — The Jade Emperor is the supreme ruler of Heaven in Chinese folk religion, governing both the divine and human realms from his celestial palace. His court mirrors a full imperial bureaucracy: he has ministers, generals, and a vast apparatus of supernatural governance.
预报	yù bào	forecast
预定	yù dìng	to book in advance; to reserve; to schedule — 预 yù (beforehand) + 定 dìng (to settle). To settle something ahead of time: a table, a room, a plan. Often written 预订 when the matter booked is goods or tickets. The 预 fixes the settling in the future.
寓意	yù yì	allegorical meaning; moral
遇见	yù jiàn	to run into, to encounter
愈来愈	yù lái yù	more and more (Taiwan variant)
元朝	Yuán cháo	Yuan dynasty
元气	yuán qì	primordial qi; vitality; the reserves of life force — 元 yuán (origin; primary; first) + 气 qì. In cosmology: the undifferentiated qi before heaven and earth separated, the primordial substrate of existence. In medicine: the constitutional qi inherited from one's parents, stored in the kidneys, spent by illness and restored by rest.
元首	yuán shǒu	head of state
元宵节	Yuán xiāo Jié	Lantern Festival
原来	yuán lái	originally; as it turns out; so that's how it is — 原 yuán (original; the root; where something came from) + 来 lái (came from; arrived from). "From the original state," used in two senses. Temporal: originally, at first (他原来住在北京 = He originally lived in Beijing). Revelatory: "so that's how it is / now I understand" (原来如此！= So that's the reason!).
原来如此	yuán lái rú cǐ	"Oh, so that's how it is!" or "I see now — "Oh, so that's how it is!" or "I see now." The classic "aha" of comprehension. The pieces have just clicked together. Slightly literary in feel but used constantly in everyday speech. The looser 原来是这样 (yuánlái shì zhèyàng) is the more colloquial version.
原形	yuán xíng	original form; true shape (often the one revealed) — 原 yuán (original) + 形 xíng. The original form a thing had before it was disguised or altered. The vivid idiom 原形毕露 yuánxíng bìlù means "the true shape is fully exposed," said when a deception finally collapses and someone is seen for what they really are.
原因	yuán yīn	cause; reason — 原 yuán (origin; source) + 因 yīn (cause). The standard noun for the cause or reason behind something: 失败的原因 "the reason for the failure." Its pair is 结果 jiéguǒ, the result.
原因分析	yuán yīn fēn xī	cause analysis — The first thing to ask for. 根本原因 (gēnběn yuányīn) is the root cause; an answer like 工人操作不当 (worker error) usually is not one. Ask why the process allowed the error.
原则上同意	yuán zé shang tóng yì	agree in principle — Signals agreement on direction while keeping the details open. Useful when the boss pushes for a handshake before the numbers are settled.
圆明园	Yuán míng yuán	Old Summer Palace (burned 1860)
袁世凯	Yuán Shì kǎi	military strongman who hijacked the republic
缘分未尽	yuán fèn wèi jìn	the karmic connection is not yet exhausted; there is still fate between us — 未 wèi = not yet; 尽 jìn = exhausted, used up. The karmic thread still has length to run , the connection between two people has not reached its natural conclusion.
缘分已尽	yuán fèn yǐ jìn	the karmic connection is exhausted; the fate between us has run its course — 已 yǐ = already; the connection has used up its allotted length. A peaceful, fatalistic way to accept a relationship ending , romantic, platonic, or professional.
缘分与命运	yuán fèn yǔ mìng yùn	fate vs. destiny — predestined connection vs. decreed outcome — 缘分 yuánfèn (predestined affinity; see the dedicated entry) and 命运 mìngyùn (fate) are related but distinct. 缘分 is about connections between people, encounters that were meant to be. 命运 is about one's overall life trajectory, the arc of what happens.
缘故	yuáng ù	reason; cause; the why behind something — 缘 (yuán, cause, affinity, the edge along which things connect) + 故 (cause, reason). A two-character word for the reason behind an event, slightly more formal and reflective than the everyday 原因 (yuányīn).
源头	yuán tóu	Source, literally "source head — Source, literally "source head." The Yangtze's source was definitively surveyed only in the 1970s–80s, deep in the Tanggula Mountains on the Tibetan Plateau. The identification of a river's 源头 carries cosmological weight; knowing where a river begins is knowing something fundamental about the world.
远处	yuǎn chù	in the distance; a distant place — 远 yuǎn (far) + 处 chù (place; location). The place that is far away, viewed from where you stand. A positional noun used as a subject or object, always indicating a vague far-off point rather than a named destination.
远大	yuǎn dà	ambitious; far-reaching; grand (of goals or ideals) — 远 yuǎn (far) + 大 dà (great; large). Applied to goals, plans, and ideals that extend far into the future or require enormous scope to realize.
远方	yuǎn fāng	a distant place; far-off land; the faraway — 远 yuǎn (far) + 方 fāng (direction; region; place). More evocative than 远处: 远方 carries a tone of longing or aspiration. Where 远处 names a physical spot in view, 远方 names a horizon you are drawn toward. Common in poetry, lyrics, and travel writing.
远古	yuǎng ǔ	remote antiquity; the distant ancient past — 远 yuǎn (far, remote) + 古 gǔ (ancient). The very distant past, the dim and often legendary beginnings before clear historical record: 远古时代 "remote antiquity," 远古传说 "ancient myths and legends." Reaches further back than 古代, toward the edge of memory.
远见	yuǎn jiàn	foresight, long-range vision
远离	yuǎn lí	to keep far from; to stay away from; to leave behind — 远 yuǎn (far) + 离 lí (to leave; to separate from). A deliberate act of putting distance between yourself and something: a place, a person, a habit. Carries volition. Used in health campaigns (远离烟酒, stay away from tobacco and alcohol), personal advice, and literature.
远亲	yuǎn qīn	distant relative; far-off kin — 远 yuǎn (distant) + 亲 qīn (kin; close; intimate). A relative at the outer edge of the family network.
远山	yuǎn shān	distant mountains
愿望	yuàn wàng	wish; aspiration
愿意	yuàn yì	to be willing; to want to — 愿 yuàn (to wish) + 意 yì (intent). The willingness of the heart to do something: 我愿意帮你 "I'm willing to help you." It expresses consent and readiness, not mere ability.
月饼	yu è bǐng	mooncake — 月 yuè + 饼 bǐng (flat cake; pastry). The round cake eaten during Mid-Autumn Festival, shaped to mirror the full moon. Traditional fillings include lotus seed paste and salted egg yolk (representing the moon).
月光	yu è guāng	moonlight — 月 yuè + 光 guāng (light; beam; glory). Moonlight. One of the most evocative words in Chinese poetry , from Du Fu to Xu Zhimo, moonlight is the quintessential image of homesickness, longing, and beauty.
月老	Yu è lǎo	the Old Man Under the Moon; deity of marriage and romantic fate — 月 yuè (moon) + 老 lǎo (old; elderly; venerable). Yuèlǎo appears at night under the moon, checking his celestial book of destined marriages, and tying the red threads that will unite couples across any distance. 拜月老 (to pray to Yuèlǎo) is a common practice among those seeking romantic fate.
月亮	yu è liàng	the moon (colloquial) — 月 yuè + 亮 liàng (bright; to shine). The bright moon , the standard colloquial word for "the moon." More grounded and everyday than the poetic 明月 míngyuè. 看月亮 "to look at the moon" · 月亮出来了 "the moon has come out."
岳飞	Yu è Fēi	City God of Hangzhou — the martyr general — 岳飞 (1103–1142), the Song dynasty general celebrated for his campaigns against the Jurchen Jin invaders, was executed on fabricated charges at the order of the chancellor Qin Hui.
阅读	yu è dú	to read (with comprehension); reading (as a skill) — 阅 yuè (to inspect; to review) + 读. The formal, written-register word for reading-with-understanding. The standard term in education: 阅读理解 yuèdú lǐjiě "reading comprehension," 阅读量 yuèdú liàng "amount one has read." More deliberate than 看 (to look-at) and more comprehension-focused than 读 alone.
阅历	yu è lì	life experience; seasoned knowledge of the world — 阅 yuè (to read; to review; to inspect) + 历 lì (what one has gone through). The accumulated worldly experience a person builds up over the years: the breadth of life seen and understood, not just events lived but their lessons absorbed.
粤菜	yu è cài	Cantonese cuisine — 粤 yuè (Guangdong; Canton) + 菜 cài (cuisine). The cooking of Guangdong, prized for lightness, freshness, and steaming that keeps each ingredient tasting of itself. Dim sum (点心) belongs to this tradition.
粤语	Yu è yǔ	Cantonese
越发	yu è fā	increasingly (literary)
越过	yu è guò	to cross over; to get past — 越 + 过 (guò, to pass). The most basic verb of crossing: a fence, a stream, a hurdle, a difficulty. Highly productive in both literal and figurative senses.
越界	yu è jiè	to cross a boundary; to overstep
越南	Yu èn án	Vietnam (lit. "south of Yue")
越权	yu è quán	to overstep one's authority — 越 + 权 (quán, authority; power). Acting beyond what your position permits , a serious accusation in any organization, especially in the bureaucratic hierarchies that have shaped Chinese institutional life since imperial times.
云彩	yún cai	colorful clouds; clouds (colloquial)
云层	yún céng	cloud layer; cloud cover
运动	yùn dòng	sport; exercise; to work out; a (social or political) movement — 运 yùn (to move; to transport) + 动 dòng (to move). Bodily exercise and sport: 做运动 "to exercise," 运动员 yùndòngyuán (athlete). The same word names an organized social or political movement, a mass of people set in motion.
运河	yùn hé	canal — 运 (yùn, to transport / haul) + 河 (river). A dug waterway built to carry boats and freight, a river made by labor rather than rain. The Grand Canal is 大运河 (dà yùnhé).
运气	yùn qi	luck; fortune (good or bad) — 运 yùn (fortune in motion) + 气 qì (vital energy; breath; atmosphere). Fortune as a flow of qi: luck circulates rather than sitting still. 好运气 = good luck; 坏运气 = bad luck. 运气好 = to be lucky; 靠运气 = to rely on luck.
运送	yùn sòng	to transport, convey — 运 (move, transport) plus 送 (send). To carry goods or people over a distance, the language of logistics, supply lines, and freight.
运用	yùn yòng	to apply; to put into practice; to exercise (a skill) — 运 yùn (to move; to carry; to transport; to operate) + 用 yòng (to use). To bring knowledge or skill into active operation: using what one knows in a real context. Where 使用 is about deploying a tool, 运用 is about skillfully exercising something more abstract , a theory, a method, a body of knowledge.
杂草	zá cǎo	weeds — 杂 zá (mixed; miscellaneous) + 草 cǎo (grass). The unwanted, untended grass that crowds a garden or field, the plants you pull out rather than plant. 拔杂草 "to pull weeds."
灾害	zāi hài	disaster, calamity
宰相	zǎi xiàng	prime minister (of imperial times); chief minister — 宰 zǎi (to govern; to manage) + 相 xiàng (minister). The highest official under the emperor, charged with overseeing the government. A staple figure of historical drama and idiom.
再次	zài cì	once again; once more (formal)
再见	zài jiàn	goodbye (see you again) — The forward-looking again fused to the meet verb. Internet speech numbers it 88 (bābā, "bye-bye"), and the dramatic register upgrades to 永别 for farewells meant to be final.
再三	zài sān	again and again; repeatedly; over and over — 再 zài (again; once more) + 三 sān (three). Three times and then some: the most natural adverb of repeated action in Mandarin. Appears before a verb to signal that someone did something multiple times, often with increasing emphasis or urgency.
再说	zài shuō	we'll talk about it later; let's deal with it when the time comes; moreover (discourse marker) — 再 (later; further) + 说 (to speak; to deal with). Multiple uses: (1) Deferral: 这件事以后再说 (We'll deal with this later , let's not now). Very common for postponing a conversation or decision. (2) Discourse marker meaning "moreover; besides": 再说，我也没空 (Besides, I'm not free either).
再也	zài yě	never again (with negation)
再者	zài zhě	furthermore; in addition; moreover (formal transition) — 再 (again; further; additionally) + 者. A discourse connector used in formal writing and spoken argument to introduce an additional point: "and there is also this." More formal than 另外 lìngwài (besides) and slightly more deliberate in pacing than 而且 érqiě (moreover).
在乎	zài hu	to care about; to mind; to take to heart — 在 (to be present) + 乎 hū (classical particle meaning "in; within; at"). Literally "to be located within [something]": one's attention or concern is present inside something. 我不在乎 (I don't care / I don't mind) is one of the most frequent phrases in spoken Chinese.
在我看来	zài wǒ kàn lái	"In my view — "In my view." Slightly more formal than 我觉得, and more deliberately frames what follows as a personal perspective. Useful when you want to signal that you have actually considered the question, not just reacting.
在一起	zài yì qǐ	together (in one place); as a couple — With 在, 一起 marks being gathered in one place: 我们住在一起 ("we live together"), 把书放在一起 ("put the books together"). It also carries the romantic sense of being a couple: 他们在一起了 ("they're together now / they're dating").
在于	zài yú	to lie in; to rest with; to consist in — 在 zài (to be at) + 于 yú (at). Points to where the heart of a matter resides: 问题在于 "the problem lies in," 关键在于 "the key rests with." A staple of explanatory and argumentative prose.
葬礼	zàng lǐ	funeral ceremony; burial rites — 葬 zàng (to bury; burial , the character shows plants 艹 and 死 death: vegetation covering the dead, returning them to the earth) + 礼 lǐ (rite; ceremony).
灶神	Zào shén	the Kitchen God — divine household reporter — The Kitchen God (also 灶王 Zàowáng or 灶君 Zàojūn) resides in the kitchen and observes the family's behavior throughout the year. On the 23rd of the 12th lunar month (one week before the new year) he ascends to Heaven to make his annual report to the Jade Emperor.
灶王爷	zào wáng yé	The Kitchen God , the divine household official who observes the family year-round and reports to the Jade Emperor before the Spring Festival. Propitiated with sweet foods before his image is burned and he ascends to make his report. A new image is installed when he returns on New Year's Eve.
造句	zào jù	to make a sentence; to compose a sentence — 造 zào (to make; to build) + 句 jù (sentence). The classroom exercise of building a sentence to practice a new word, a verb-object compound: 用 "因为" 造句 "make a sentence with 'because'."
噪音	zào yīn	noise — 噪 (clamor, wearing three mouths) + 音. The urban complaint word: construction 噪音, traffic 噪音, and the neighbor's renovation drill. 噪音污染 (noise pollution) is a recognized legal complaint category in Chinese cities.
怎么 + 动词	zěn me + ve r b	how (to do something); in what way — The core use: placed before a verb, 怎么 asks about the method or manner of an action. 怎么走 ("how to get there"), 怎么说 ("how to say it"), 怎么用 ("how to use it").
怎么说呢	zěn me shuō ne	"How should I put it…" Buys a moment while signaling that you are searching for the right phrasing. Implies you have a thought but are weighing how to express it, which sounds thoughtful rather than blank. Useful before delivering a nuanced opinion.
怎么样	zěn me yàng	how is it; how about it — The evaluating cousin of 怎么. It asks about a state or opinion rather than a method: 这家餐厅怎么样？("how's this restaurant?"), 你最近怎么样？("how have you been?"). It also floats a suggestion: 我们去看电影，怎么样？("let's see a movie, how about it?"). Negated, 不怎么样 means "nothing special, so-so".
怎么走？	zěn me zǒu ?	How do I get there? / Which way? — asking for directions — 怎么 zěnme (how; what way) + 走 zǒu (to go). The standard question for asking directions , "How do I get to X?" Response patterns: 一直走 yīzhí zǒu (go straight), 左转 zuǒzhuǎn (turn left), 右转 yòuzhuǎn (turn right), 过了红绿灯 guò le hónglǜdēng (past the traffic light). 往哪边走？= which direction to go?
怎样	zěn yàng	how; in what way; what about — 怎 zěn (how) + 样 yàng (manner). Asks after the manner or outcome of something: 这件事你打算怎样处理 "how do you plan to handle this?" Close to 怎么 zěnme, slightly more formal.
赠送	zèng sòng	to present, give as a gift — 赠 (bestow, present) plus 送 (give). A formal compound for presenting something gratis, common in commerce and ceremony: free gifts with purchase, donated copies, complimentary tickets.
炸鸡	zhá jī	fried chicken — 炸 (zhá, to deep-fry) + 鸡 (chicken). The crisp street-food and fast-food staple, often eaten with 啤酒 (píjiǔ, beer) in the Korean-style 炸鸡啤酒 pairing.
展览馆	zhǎn lǎng uǎn	exhibition hall — 展览 zhǎnlǎn (to exhibit) + 馆. The hall where exhibitions are mounted, cousin to the 博物馆 but temporary in what it shows.
展望	zhǎn wàng	to look ahead; outlook
占有	zhàn yǒu	to possess; to occupy
战国	Zhàng uó	the Warring States period
战国策	Zhàng uó Cè	Stratagems of the Warring States — the source text
战争前的仪式	zhàn zhēng qián de yí shì	pre-battle ritual — the shaman as military consultant — Before major military campaigns, Tungusic and Mongolian rulers consulted their shamans , divining the auspiciousness of the timing, the direction of attack, and the likely outcome.
站点	zhàn diǎn	site; node; stop — 站 (station) + 点 (diǎn, point): a designated point or node, whether a physical service point or a website. Broad and slightly technical, common in logistics, networks, and field operations.
站岗	zhàng ǎng	to stand guard — 站 (to stand) + 岗 (gǎng, a post or sentry position): to take up a guard post. A verb-object phrase, literally "to stand a post," used of soldiers, guards, and watchmen holding their station.
站立	zhàn lì	to stand erect — 站 (stand) + 立 (stand): two near-synonyms stacked for emphasis, a written-register word for standing upright. More formal than plain 站, common in instructions, ceremonies, and description.
站起来	zhàn qǐ lái	to stand up — 站 + 起来 (the directional complement "up"): to rise from sitting to standing. The 起来 makes the verb a completed upward motion rather than a static posture.
站台	zhàn tái	platform — 站 (station) + 台 (tái, raised platform): the boarding platform at a station, the raised edge alongside the track. By extension, 站台 also means to publicly back someone, to "stand on the platform" for them.
站长	zhàn zhǎng	station chief; webmaster — 站 (station) + 长 (zhǎng, head, chief): the person in charge of a station. Originally a stationmaster; now also the administrator of a 网站, a webmaster.
张望	zhāng wàng	to look around; to peer about — 张 zhāng (to open, to spread) + 望 wàng (to look). To look around searchingly, the eyes opened wide and turning in every direction: 四处张望 "to look all around." It carries a note of uncertainty or expectation, as of someone scanning a crowd for a face.
章节	zhāng jié	chapters and sections (of a book) — 章 zhāng (chapter) + 节 jié (section). The structural divisions of a written work taken together. A book's text is segmented into 章 and 节 the way a stalk is segmented by its knots.
长安	Cháng ān	Chang'an, the Tang capital
长辈	zhǎng bèi	senior generation
长城内外	cháng chéng nèi wài	inside and outside the Great Wall; the agricultural vs. steppe world — A geographic and cultural formula that names the two worlds the wall divided: the settled, grain-farming Han civilization inside, and the pastoral, nomadic cultures of the steppe outside. 内外 encodes not just geography but an entire worldview about civilization and its boundaries.
长短	cháng duǎn	length; the long and short of it — 长 (cháng, long) bound to 短 (duǎn, short): a paired opposite naming the dimension of length itself. Figuratively it means the rights and wrongs, or any unforeseen mishap.
长江	Cháng Jiāng	the Yangtze River — lit. "the long river" — 长 cháng (long) + 江 jiāng (large river; river south of Huai River). The Yangtze, Asia's longest river at 6,300 km, is simply "the Long River." Compare: 黄河 Huáng Hé (Yellow River) is named for its color; 长江 is named for its length.
长平之战	Cháng Píng zhī Zhàn	Battle of Changping (260 BCE) — the decisive blow against Zhao — The largest and most catastrophic battle of the Warring States period. Qin and Zhao forces fought for three years in the Shangdang region (modern Shanxi) before Zhao replaced its cautious commander 廉颇 Lián Pō with the aggressive 赵括 Zhào Kuò, a general who knew military theory but had never commanded…
长期合作	cháng qī hé zuò	long-term cooperation — The phrase that justifies concessions on both sides: the factory gives on price for the sake of future orders, you give on terms for the sake of a stable partner. Invoke it when asking for something; hear it as a request when the other side uses it.
长生	cháng shēng	immortality; long life
长寿	cháng shòu	longevity; long life
涨价	zhǎng jià	to raise the price
丈夫	zhàng fu	husband — 丈 zhàng (an honorific for an adult man) + 夫 fū (man). The ordinary, neutral word for one's husband, the man one is married to. In older usage 大丈夫 dà zhàngfu also means a true man, a man of character, but on its own 丈夫 simply names the spouse.
找到	zhǎo dào	to find; to locate — 找 zhǎo (to search for; to look for) + 到 dào (arrive). Searching that arrived at its target: the thing was found. 找 alone is the act of searching; 找到 is the confirmed discovery. 找不到 (can't find it) and 找到了 (found it!) are extremely high-frequency in daily speech.
找工作	zhǎo gōng zuò	to look for a job; to job-hunt — The set phrase for job-hunting. 找 (to look for) plus 工作. Common in life and conversation, especially among graduates and people changing roles: 毕业以后我要找工作 ("after I graduate I'll look for a job"). The result of a successful search is 找到工作 ("found a job"), with 到 marking the achieved result.
赵州狗子	Zhào zhōu gǒu zi	Zhaozhou's dog — the gateway kōan of Chinese Chan — Master Zhaozhou Congshen 赵州从谂 (778–897 CE) was asked: "Does a dog have Buddha nature?" He replied: 无 wú. Since Buddhist doctrine holds that all sentient beings have Buddha nature, "no" is doctrinally wrong , but so is "yes" if it's merely conceptual.
照明	zhào míng	illumination; lighting (noun &amp; verb) — 照 zhào (to shine upon; to illuminate) + 明 míng (bright). Used for artificial lighting systems, stage lighting, and the act of shining a light on something. 照明设备 = lighting equipment.
照相	zhào xiàng	to take a photograph — 照 zhào (to shine; to reflect) + 相 xiàng (appearance). To fix a likeness in a picture: 给我照相 "take a photo of me." A separable verb: 照了一张相 "took one photo."
折子戏	zhé zi xì	Individual scenes — Individual scenes: excerpts from longer 昆曲 dramas performed as self-contained pieces. As the full-length drama tradition declined, individual scenes that are particularly beautiful or dramatically concentrated became the standard performance unit.
这不是嘛	zhè bú shì ma	isn't this exactly it / this is clearly the case
这倒未必	zhè dào wèi bì	"That's not necessarily so — "That's not necessarily so." A more literary pushback, often used in discussions or debates. 倒 marks the contrary tone; 未必 means "not necessarily." Slightly considered, signals careful disagreement.
这个	zhè ge	this; this one — 这 zhè (this) + 个 ge. The demonstrative "this one," with 个 supplying the classifier slot. Its pair is 那个 nàge (that one). Often heard as a filler too, like an English "um."
这个嘛	zhè ge ma	"Well, this…" or "as for this…" The 嘛 particle gives the phrase a casual, considering tone. Often used to introduce a response to a question that does not have a simple answer. Roughly: "well, about that…"
这回	zhè huí	this time; on this occasion — 这 zhè (this) + 回 huí (time). The colloquial "this time," interchangeable with 这次 zhè cì but a touch more casual: 这回我一定赢 "this time I'll win for sure."
这就是为什么	zhè jiù shì wèi shén me	"That's why — "That's why." Used after explaining a cause to land the consequence with emphasis. 这就是为什么我不喜欢他 ("that's why I don't like him"). Slightly emphatic; signals you have just arrived at the punchline.
这里	zhè lǐ	here
这里 · 那里	zhè lǐ nà lǐ	here · there — 这 (zhè, this) + 里 (interior space) = 这里 (this place, here). 那 (nà, that) + 里 = 那里 (that place, there).
这么说吧	zhè me shuō ba	"Let me put it this way — "Let me put it this way." A colloquial reframing marker, used when you are about to take another run at explaining something. The 吧 particle softens it and invites the listener to follow you into the next attempt.
这样	zhè yàng	like this; this way; so; in this manner — 这 zhè (this) + 样 yàng (manner). Points at a way of being or doing close at hand: 这样做 "do it like this," 就这样吧 "let it be this way, then."
浙菜	Zhè cài	Zhejiang Cuisine
着急	zháo jí	to worry, to feel anxious — 着 (zháo, to be caught by) + 急 (urgency). To be seized by anxiety. This is the inward state of 急: a fretting heart, not a fast body. It is the most common everyday word for feeling worried over something time-sensitive.
着急上火	zháo jí shàng huǒ	frantic with worry
着落	zhuó luò	a place to land; a resolution
针眼	zhēn yǎn	the eye of a needle; (medical) sty — 针 zhēn (needle) + 眼. The hole in a sewing needle , the same metaphor English uses. Also a colloquial term for a sty on the eyelid (the small swelling looking like a tiny eye).
真不容易	zhēn bù róng yì	that's really not easy; well done — Standard expression of admiration or sympathy for someone who has overcome difficulty: a graduation, a long project, raising children. The 真 makes it heartfelt rather than perfunctory.
真诚	zhēn chéng	sincere, in earnest (in attitude or expression) — 真 zhēn + 诚 chéng (sincerity; the Confucian virtue of inner-outer alignment). Sincere in attitude: an apology, a wish, a smile, a thank-you that is not just formal courtesy but actually meant. The diplomatic and written register.
真的假的	zhēn de jiǎ de	"Seriously?" Literally "true or fake," used as an emphatic version of 真的吗 when something sounds surprising or hard to believe. Common among younger speakers and friends; slightly informal for use with elders or in professional settings.
真的吗	zhēn de ma	really? for real? — The most common follow-up question in casual conversation, expressing surprise. 真的 on its own answers it: "Yes, really." Often softened to 真假 (zhēn jiǎ, "real or fake?") in playful or informal speech.
真好	zhēn hǎo	really nice; truly good; that's lovely — The all-purpose appreciation. 真好! works as a stand-alone exclamation: "wonderful!" 真好的人 "a really good person." 这里真好 "this place is really nice."
真空保温	zhēn kōng bǎo wēn	vacuum insulation — Double-wall insulation: the air between liner and shell is pumped out, 抽真空 (chōu zhēnkōng). 保温 is keeping warm, 保冷 keeping cold; 保温测试 is the thermal retention test, and 保温效果 the result.
真理	zhēn lǐ	truth (philosophical, capital-T) — 真 zhēn + 理 lǐ (principle; pattern; reason). The truth in the philosophical, abstract sense , the deep principle that governs, the ultimate reality. The word used in religious, scientific, and political discourse for capital-T Truth.
真实	zhēn shí	real, factual, actually existing — 真 zhēn + 实 shí (solid; real; substance). The factual register: actually-the-case, in contrast to fabricated, fictional, or virtual. Used for stories, events, identities, statistics.
真讨厌	zhēn tǎo yàn	how annoying; ugh — Light complaint, often spoken with a sigh. The 真 marks the speaker's genuine irritation rather than a measured judgment.
真相	zhēn xiàng	the truth; the real state of affairs — 真 zhēn (true) + 相 xiàng (appearance; face). The true face of a matter once the surface is stripped away: 事情的真相 "the truth of the matter," 揭露真相 "to expose the truth."
真心	zhēn xīn	a sincere heart; from the heart (adv.) — 真 zhēn + 心 xīn (heart). Sincerity located at the heart-level: not just attitude (真诚) but the felt inner orientation. As a noun: 一片真心 "a heart full of sincerity." As an adverb: 真心爱你 "I love you from the heart."
真正	zhēn zhèng	genuine, true (the real thing, not the imitation) — 真 zhēn + 正 zhèng (correct; proper; orthodox). The genuine-article register: this is the real one, the one that lives up to the name, not the imitation. Common attributively before nouns.
阵脚	zhèn jiǎo	battle-line foundation; one's footing in a contest — 阵 zhèn (battle formation) + 脚. The foot of the battle line , the structural integrity of a position. The common idiom 乱了阵脚 luàn le zhènjiǎo "to lose one's footing" describes the moment a debater, athlete, or general is rattled and the formation collapses.
镇定	zhèn dìng	composed; calm; to keep one's cool — 镇 zhèn (to press down; to keep calm) + 定 dìng (settled). The steadiness of a person under pressure, a cool head when others panic: 保持镇定 "to stay composed," 镇定自若 "perfectly calm and self-possessed."
争论	zhēng lùn	to dispute; controversy
挣钱	zhèng qián	to earn money
拯救	zhěng jiù	to save, to deliver — 拯 (zhěng, to lift up out of) + 救 (rescue). A weightier, more literary "save," used for deliverance on a grand or moral scale: saving a soul, a people, a planet.
整个	zhěng gè	the whole; entire — 整 zhěng (whole) + 个 gè. "The whole of" something taken as one piece: 整个城市 "the whole city," 整个晚上 "the entire evening." Here 个 keeps its sense of a single complete unit.
整理	zhěng lǐ	to tidy up; to sort; to put in order — 整 zhěng (whole; to straighten) + 理 lǐ (to put in order). To arrange scattered things back into order: 整理房间 "to tidy the room," 整理笔记 "to organize one's notes."
整体	zhěng tǐ	the whole; the entirety; as a whole — 整 zhěng (whole, complete) + 体 tǐ (body). A thing taken as one integrated body rather than as separate parts. Its standing contrast is 部分 bùfen, a part: 整体利益 "the interests of the whole."
正常	zhèng cháng	normal; regular — 正 zhèng (proper; upright) + 常 cháng (ordinary). On the standard track, as things should be: 一切正常 "everything is normal." Its opposite is 反常 fǎncháng or 不正常.
正好	zhèng hǎo	just right; exactly; as it happens — 正 zhèng (exactly) + 好 hǎo (good). Landing exactly on the mark of fit or timing: 大小正好 "exactly the right size," 你来得正好 "you've come at just the right moment."
正名	zhèng míng	rectification of names; calling things by their correct names — A key political-philosophical doctrine of Confucius. When a disciple asks what he would do first if given control of a state, Confucius says: rectify names 必也正名乎.
正念	zhèng niàn	right mindfulness
正气	zhèng qì	upright qi; righteous energy; moral integrity — 正 zhèng (upright; correct; proper) + 气 qì. In TCM: the body's defensive qi that resists pathogenic invasion. In moral discourse: the upright character and courage that resists corruption and injustice.
正确	zhèng qu è	correct; right; accurate — 正 zhèng (straight; right) + 确 què (sure; firm). Correct in the sense of matching the truth or the standard: 正确答案 "the correct answer," 正确的方法 "the right method." Its opposite is 错误 cuòwù.
正式	zhèng shì	formal; official
正是	zhèng shì	precisely; exactly (formal confirmation)
正体字	zhèng tǐ zì	Traditional characters — Traditional characters: the term used in Taiwan for the traditional character system that Taiwan retained when the PRC introduced simplified characters in the 1950s. Taiwan uses 正體字 (traditional/correct form characters); PRC uses 简体字 (simplified characters).
正统	zhèng tǒng	orthodoxy; legitimate succession
正义	zhèng yì	justice; righteousness; the just cause — 正 zhèng (correct; upright; proper , the character shows a foot 止 walking toward a target 一, straight on) + 义 yì (righteousness; moral rightness). Together: righteousness that is properly aligned , justice as it should be, not merely as claimed. 正义感 zhèngyìgǎn = a sense of justice.
正在进行中	zhèng zài jìn xíng zhōng	Currently in progress; underway — A more formal and written version of the progressive, combining 正在 with 进行 jìnxíng (to carry out, to proceed) and 中 zhōng (amid, in the middle of). Common in announcements, project status updates, and written notices. 活动正在进行中 = the event is currently underway.
郑和	Zhèng Hé	admiral of the seven voyages
政治家	zhèng zhì jiā	statesman; skilled politician — 政治 zhèngzhì (politics) + 家 jiā. More elevated than 政客 zhèngkè (politician, often pejorative, implying opportunism and maneuvering). 政治家 implies vision, skill, and genuine mastery of governance: a statesman rather than a mere political operator. The 家 suffix confers dignity.
之后	zhī hòu	after; following
之间	zhī jiān	between; among (more formal) — 之 zhī (classical possessive) + 间 jiān (space between). The bookish, frequent way to say "between": 朋友之间 "between friends," 国与国之间 "between nations." It frames the space within a relationship or a set.
之前	zhī qián	before
之所以	zhī suǒ yǐ	the reason why; the cause for which
知道了	zhī dào le	got it; understood; okay — The everyday acknowledgement that you have received and registered information or an instruction. Extremely common as a one-word reply. Beware the tone: a flat or clipped 知道了 can read as impatient, like "yeah, I know already." 好的 (okay) or 明白了 (understood) are gentler alternatives.
知己	zhī jǐ	a bosom friend; one who truly knows you — 知 zhī (to know) + 己 jǐ (self). One who knows your self, the rare friend who understands you completely. The famous line 人生得一知己足矣 holds that to gain a single true friend in life is enough.
知名	zhī míng	well-known; famous; noted — 知 zhī (to know; to be known) + 名 míng (name; fame; renown). Literally: one whose name is known. 知名 sits in the formal-written register; everyday speech prefers 有名 yǒumíng (has fame) or 出名 chūmíng (name has come out). 知名度 zhīmíngdù = degree of fame, public profile.
知青	zhī qīng	educated sent-down youth
知识	zhī shi	knowledge; information; factual learning — 知 zhī (to know; to understand) + 识 shí (to recognize; to discern; knowledge gained through recognition). Factual, storable, transmissible knowledge , what fills textbooks, databases, and examinations. 知识分子 zhīshi fènzǐ (intellectual; educated person , lit.
知识产权	zhī shi chǎn quán	intellectual property
知音	zhī yīn	soulmate; the one who truly understands — From Boya and Ziqi: one who knows your tone. Weightier than 朋友 (friend); to call someone 知音 claims they understand what you mean beneath what you say. The lament 知音难觅 ("a zhiyin is hard to find") is the cultured way to say good friends are rare.
知者	zhī zhě	the one who knows; the wise person
知足	zhī zú	knowing sufficiency; contentment with enough — 知 zhī (to know) + 足 zú (sufficient; foot; fullness). One of the Daodejing's most politically charged concepts: knowing when one has enough, and stopping there. The opposite of insatiable accumulation.
执行	zhí xíng	to execute; to enforce; to carry out (an order, a plan, a sentence) — 执 zhí (to grasp; to hold) + 行 xíng. To grasp-and-act. The formal verb for executing , orders, contracts, court rulings, software programs. 执行命令 "carry out an order"; 执行任务 "carry out a mission"; 执行总裁 (CEO) , literally "executing chief manager."
直角	zhí jiǎo	right angle
直接	zhí jiē	direct, directly — 直 (zhí, straight) + 接 (join). The two ends meet with nothing in between, a straight join. As an adverb it means doing a thing with no go-between, no detour.
职业	zhí yè	occupation; profession; vocational — 职 zhí (post; duty) + 业 yè (work). The line of work a person practices for a living: 职业选择 "choice of profession." As a modifier it means professional or vocational: 职业运动员 "professional athlete," 职业学校 "vocational school."
职业道德	zhí yè dào dé	professional ethics; occupational morality; the moral standards specific to a role — 职业 zhíyè (occupation; profession; vocation) + 道德. The morality that attaches specifically to a role , what it means to be a good doctor, journalist, teacher, or official, as distinct from merely following the general rules of society.
植物	zhí wù	plant
只有才	zhǐ yǒu cái	only if…then (necessary condition)
纸钱	zhǐ qián	spirit money — currency for the afterlife — 纸钱 (also 冥纸 míngzhǐ, 金纸 jīnzhǐ in Taiwan, or 冥币 míngbì) are paper facsimiles of money and goods burnt as offerings; the smoke carries them to the dead.
指明方向	zhǐ míng fāng xiàng	to point out the direction; to provide guidance — 指 (zhǐ, to point) + 明 (míng, clear) + 方向. The fixed phrase for guidance from a teacher, leader, or authority. Common in educational and political registers , a teacher 为学生指明方向, a leader 为国家指明方向. Carries a slightly elevated, often exhortatory tone.
指南针	zhǐn án zhēn	compass (the navigational instrument) — 指 (to point) + 南 (south) + 针 (needle). A south-pointing needle: the Chinese compass was designed to point south rather than north, in keeping with the cosmological primacy of the south.
指示代词	zhǐ shì dài cí	demonstrative pronoun (这/那/哪)
至少	zhì shǎo	at least — 至 zhì (to reach; at the extreme of) + 少 (few, little). At the minimum: "reaching the least amount." 至少要三天 (it'll take at least three days); 至少有一百人 (at least a hundred people). The counterpart is 至多 zhìduō (at most). 至少 sets a floor; 至多 sets a ceiling.
至于	zhì yú	as for
志向	zhì xiàng	aspiration; ambition; the goal one is set on — 志 zhì (will; resolve) + 向 xiàng (direction). The direction of one's will, what one aspires to: 远大的志向 "lofty aspirations." The facing of ambition, where a person has set their life.
制品	zhì pǐn	manufactured article; processed product
治病	zhì bìng	healing — the shaman's primary function — The most common reason a community calls a shaman is illness. In shamanic cosmology, sickness typically results from one of three spirit-world causes: soul loss (魂魄丢失 húnpò diūshī , the soul has been captured by a spirit or wandered away in fright), spirit intrusion (邪灵侵入 xiélíng qīnrù , a harmful s…
质量	zhì liàng	quality: how good something is (also physical mass) — 质 zhì (substance, nature) + 量 liàng (measure). In everyday speech 质量 is quality, the standard or grade of a product or piece of work: 质量好 (good quality), 提高质量 (to raise quality). In physics the same word is the technical term for mass. Context separates the two cleanly.
质问	zhì wèn	to interrogate
致富	zhì fù	to get rich; to make a fortune — 致 (to bring about, to arrive at) plus 富 (wealth). To become wealthy, especially through one's own effort. 勤劳致富 (qínláo zhìfù), getting rich through diligence, is a stock phrase.
智力	zhì lì	intelligence; intellectual capacity; mental power — 智 zhì (wisdom; intellect) + 力 lì (power; force; strength). Intelligence framed as a measurable force: the mental capacity that can be applied, trained, and compared. 智力测试 zhìlì cèshì = intelligence test. 智力开发 zhìlì kāifā = intellectual development (especially of children).
智商	zhì shāng	IQ; intelligence quotient — 智 zhì (intelligence) + 商 shāng (quotient , in mathematics, the result of division; also: commerce, suggesting calculation).
智者	zhì zhě	the wise person; one who possesses wisdom
智者乐水，仁者乐山	zhì zhě lè shuǐ , rén zhě lè shān	the wise take joy in water; the benevolent take joy in mountains — Lúnyǔ 6.23. The locus classicus of the 山水 dyad. 乐 is read lè (to take joy in) here , the older causative/affective reading. The couplet pairs water with 智 (wisdom , adaptive, flowing, responsive) and mountains with 仁 (benevolence , enduring, supporting, still).
中国话	Zhōng guó huà	Chinese (the language, casual)
中国梦	Zhōng guó mèng	the Chinese Dream
中国人	Zhōng guó rén	Chinese person
中国是礼仪之邦	Zhōng guó shì lǐ yí zhī bāng	China is a nation of ritual and propriety — A classical phrase of national self-identification: China sees itself as the civilization that most completely developed and transmitted the principles of ritual propriety. Used in cultural pride contexts and historical writing. 礼仪之邦 = "a land of ritual propriety."
中华	Zhōng huá	China (cultural/civilizational sense)
中华民国	Zhōng huá Míng uó	Republic of China
中间	zhōng jiān	middle; center; in between; among — 中 zhōng (center) + 间 jiān (space). The space in the middle, whether of a row, a room, or a stretch of time: 坐在中间 "to sit in the middle," 在两座山中间 "between two mountains."
中秋拜月	Zhōng qiū Bài Yu è	Mid-Autumn — Moon Offerings — The Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节 Zhōngqiū Jié), 15th day of the 8th lunar month, centers on honoring the moon (月亮 yuèliàng) and the moon goddess 嫦娥 Cháng'é, who fled to the moon after drinking the elixir of immortality.
中秋节	Zhōng qiū jié	Mid-Autumn Festival
中文系	zhōng wén xì	department of Chinese (at a university) — 中文 zhōngwén (Chinese language) + 系 xì (department). The Chinese department of a university. The bare 系 is the academic department itself, so any field plugs in front of it: 数学系 math department, 法律系 law department.
中午	zhōng wǔ	noon
中心	zhōng xīn	center; central point; hub — 中 zhōng (middle) + 心 xīn (heart). Lit. "middle heart." The conceptual and physical center of something: a city, an argument, an organization. Used freely in both spatial and abstract senses. Extremely productive in compound formation: any institution can become a 中心 by adding its domain.
中药	zhōng yào	Chinese herbal medicine — 中 zhōng (Chinese) + 药 yào (medicine; drug). Chinese herbal medicine: the pharmacological branch of TCM. The classical formulary contains thousands of substances: plant-based (ginseng 人参 rénshēn, astragalus 黄芪 huángqí, wolfberry 枸杞 gǒuqǐ), mineral (cinnabar 朱砂 zhūshā), and animal-derived.
中庸	zhōng yōng	the Doctrine of the Mean
中元节	Zhōng yuán Jié	the Ghost Festival — Daoist name for the 15th of the 7th month — 中 zhōng (middle) + 元 yuán (origin; first; primary) + 节 jié (festival; season). The Daoist name, derived from the Three Officials calendar: 上元 (upper prime, 1st month, 15th), 中元 (middle prime, 7th month, 15th), 下元 (lower prime, 10th month, 15th). Each 元 is the birthday of one official.
中原	Zhōng yuán	Central Plains; the heartland — The Central Plain , the heartland of the Yellow River basin, corresponding broadly to modern Henan province and adjacent areas. To "take the Central Plain" (逐鹿中原 zhú lù Zhōngyuán, "chase the deer across the Central Plain") is a classical idiom for competing for control of China.
终点站	zhōng diǎn zhàn	terminus; last stop — 终点 (zhōngdiǎn, end point) + 站 (stop): the final stop on a route, where the line ends and everyone gets off. Its opposite is 起点站 qǐdiǎnzhàn, the first stop.
种地	zhòng dì	to till the land
种子	zhǒng zi	seed (of a plant); (sports) seeded player — 种 zhǒng (kind; to sow) + 子 zi. The seed sense of 子 made explicit. By extension it names a "seeded" competitor in a tournament, the one expected to grow into a winner.
众妙之门也	zhòng miào zhī mén yě	the gate of all wonders (Daodejing 1, closing)
众生	zhòng shēng	all sentient beings
重点	zhòng diǎn	key point; focus; emphasis; priority — 重 zhòng (heavy; important) + 点 diǎn (point). The heavy point, the part that matters most. 重点大学 "key universities," 划重点 "to mark the key points," the things to underline.
重点是	zhòng diǎn shì	"The point is" or "the main thing is — "The point is" or "the main thing is." Close cousin to 关键在于, slightly more conversational. Often used to refocus a discussion that has drifted: 重点是, 我们要不要去 ("the point is, are we going or not").
重读	chóng dú / zhòng dú	to re-read (chóng); to stress (a syllable, zhòng) — 重 + 读 , but 重 is a polyphone. chóngdú = "again-read," to re-read a book or article. zhòngdú = "heavy-read," to stress or accent a syllable in pronunciation. Same characters, different reading, different meaning entirely.
重复	chóng fù	to repeat; to duplicate; repetition — 重 chóng (again) + 复 fù (to return; again). To do or say the same thing over: 重复一遍 "to repeat once more." Note the chóng reading: a common error is to read it zhòng.
重量	zhòng liàng	weight (the physical quantity) — 重 zhòng (heavy) + 量 liàng (quantity; measure). The amount of heaviness, weight as measured: 重量很轻 "the weight is light." The bodily version is 体重 tǐzhòng, one's body weight.
重视	zhòng shì	to value; to attach importance to; to take seriously — 重 zhòng (to weigh heavily) + 视 shì (to regard; to view). To treat something as carrying weight, to give it due attention: 重视教育 "to value education." Its opposite is 忽视 hūshì, to overlook.
重心	zhòng xīn	center of gravity; focus; emphasis — 重 zhòng (heavy; weight) + 心 xīn (heart; center). A physics term that has crossed fully into metaphorical use: where the weight of attention, effort, or strategic priority lies. Used in business planning, policy discussions, and personal goal-setting.
重新	chóng xīn	anew; afresh; once more (from the start) — 重 chóng (again) + 新 xīn (new). To do something over from a fresh start: 重新开始 "to start anew," 重新考虑 "to reconsider." Stronger than a plain 又, it implies a clean slate.
重阳	Chóng yáng	Double Ninth; Double Yang — the festival name — 重 chóng (double; repeated; layered) + 阳 yáng (yang; the masculine creative principle; odd numbers; heaven). The name describes the cosmological condition of the date: two nine-yang numbers coinciding.
重阳糕	Chóng yáng gāo	Double Ninth cake — the city dweller substitution — 重阳 Chóngyáng (the festival) + 糕 gāo (cake; steamed or baked confection). The cleverest detail of the festival: 糕 (gāo, cake) is homophonous with 高 (gāo, high).
重阳节	Chóng yáng Jié	Double Ninth Festival (autumn)
重要	zhòng yào	important; significant — 重 zhòng (heavy; weighty; important) + 要 (essential; necessary). 重要 means "important" in the sense of having significant weight or consequence. One of the most common adjectives in Chinese. 非常重要 (extremely important) · 最重要的是… (Most importantly…).
重要性	zhòng yào xìng	importance
周朝	Zhōu Cháo	the Zhou dynasty
周公	Zhōu gōng	Duke of Zhou
珠心算	zhū xīn suàn	Abacus mental arithmetic — Abacus mental arithmetic: performing suanpan calculations by visualizing the instrument in the mind. Neurologically distinct from verbal mental arithmetic: brain imaging shows practitioners use visuospatial rather than language regions.
诸子百家	zhū zǐ bǎi jiā	Hundred Schools of Thought
猪八戒	zhū bā jiè	Zhu Bajie — the pig, comic appetite — A former marshal of Heaven banished into a pig's body for misconduct, ruled by his appetites for food, sleep, and women, lazy, cowardly, and always scheming to abandon the quest. Yet he is also warm, funny, and ultimately faithful.
猪肉	zhū ròu	pork — 猪 (zhū, pig) + 肉 (meat). The most-eaten meat in China, so common that 肉 alone often means pork by default in recipes.
竹简	zhú jiǎn	bamboo writing slip
竹林七贤	Zhú lín Qī Xián	Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove
主持	zhǔ chí	to host; to preside over; to chair — 主 zhǔ (to preside) + 持 chí (to hold). To run an event from the chair: to host a show, chair a meeting, or take charge of a project. The host of a broadcast is a 主持人 zhǔchírén.
主动	zhǔ dòng	to take the initiative; proactive; of one's own accord — 主 zhǔ (master; to take charge) + 动 dòng (to act). To move first and on one's own, rather than waiting to be pushed. Its opposite is 被动 bèidòng (passive). 主动帮忙 "to help without being asked."
主观	zhǔ guān	subjective
主角	zhǔ ju é	protagonist; main character
主权	zhǔ quán	sovereignty
主人	zhǔ rén	master; owner; host — 主 zhǔ (master) + 人 rén (person). The one who owns a thing or receives a guest: an animal's owner, a house's master, the host of a gathering. Its pair is 客人 kèrén, the guest.
主食	zhǔ shí	Staple food — Staple food: the rice, noodles, or dumplings served at the end of a Chinese meal. The late arrival of the staple signals that the banquet was generous enough that no one needed to fill up on carbohydrates.
主题	zhǔ tí	theme; central subject; motif — 主 zhǔ (main; principal) + 题 tí (theme). The central idea that organizes a work, an event, or a piece of music: 电影的主题 "the theme of the film," 主题公园 "a theme park." It is the heading that everything else serves.
主体	zhǔ tǐ	subject, agent
主位	zhǔ wèi	The seat of honor at a table — The seat of honor at a table: typically facing the door, with one's back to the kitchen or wall. Assigning the 主位 to the senior guest or the person being celebrated is a face-giving act.
主席	zhǔ xí	chairman; chairperson; president (of a body) — 主 zhǔ (presiding) + 席 xí (seat; mat). Literally "the presiding seat," the one who sits at the head of a meeting or a state. Used for the chair of a committee and for a head of state.
主要	zhǔ yào	main; primary; principal — 主 zhǔ (master; host; main; primary) + 要 (essential). "The main/essential one." Used to identify the principal element among several: 主要问题 (the main problem) · 主要原因 (the primary reason) · 主要目标 (the primary goal). Common in analysis, journalism, and academic writing.
主意	zhǔ yi	idea; plan; decision — 主 zhǔ (governing) + 意 yì (intention). The plan one settles on, the idea one acts by: 好主意 "a good idea," 拿主意 "to make up one's mind." Note the neutral tone on yi.
主张	zhǔ zhāng	to advocate; to maintain; a stance; a position — 主 zhǔ (to decide) + 张 zhāng (to stretch; to spread). As a verb, to put forward and stand by a view; as a noun, the view itself: 我主张和平 "I advocate peace," 这是我的主张 "this is my position."
煮蛋	zhǔ dàn	boiled egg
助手	zhù shǒu	assistant; helper
注定	zhù dìng	destined; fated
注脚	zhù jiǎo	footnote; gloss; annotation — 注 zhù (to annotate; to gloss) + 脚. Annotation at the foot of the page. A more elegant alternative to the modern compound 脚注 jiǎozhù (which has the same components in reverse order).
注目	zhù mù	to fix one's gaze; to give attention to — 注 (to pour into; to concentrate) + 目 (eye). To concentrate the eye on something. A formal register word for focused attention: 引人注目 yǐn rén zhùmù means "eye-catching" or "attention-drawing."
注意	zhù yì	to pay attention; to take note; to watch out — 注 zhù (to pour; to fix) + 意 yì (notion; attention). To pour the mind onto something, that is, to pay attention: 注意安全 "mind your safety," 请注意 "please take note."
祝福	zhù fú	to bless; to wish someone well; best wishes — 祝 zhù (to wish; to pray for) + 福 fú (blessing). To send blessings to someone, as a verb or noun. 送上我的祝福 = "I send you my best wishes." Standard in holiday messages, weddings, and farewells.
抓紧	zhuā jǐn	grasp firmly; make the most of (time) — 抓 (zhuā, to grab) + 紧 (tight). To grab and hold with no slack. Literally to grip something hard, figuratively to seize time and not waste it: 抓紧时间 (zhuājǐn shíjiān), make the most of the time.
专门	zhuān mén	specialized; specially; on purpose — 专 zhuān (focused; sole) + 门 mén (field). Concentrated on one doorway. As an adjective, specialized: 专门知识 "specialized knowledge." As an adverb, specially or on purpose: 我专门来看你 "I came specially to see you."
专业	zhuān yè	major; specialty; professional, specialized — 专 zhuān (to specialize; sole) + 业 yè (field of study). As a noun, the major one studies: 我的专业是历史 "my major is history." As an adjective, professional or specialized: 专业知识 "specialized knowledge," 很专业 "very professional."
转化	zhuǎn huà	to transform; to convert; to change from one form into another — 转 zhuǎn (to turn; to shift) + 化 huà (to transform). 转化 names a conversion across a boundary: one form, type, or state turning into another. It is the standard word in science, philosophy, and economics for systematic conversion, the conditions under which A becomes B.
转换	zhuǎn huàn	to switch, convert
转经筒	zhuǎn jīng tǒng	Prayer wheel — Prayer wheel: a cylindrical object containing mantras, rotated clockwise by practitioners. Each rotation is considered equivalent to reciting the mantra contained within.
转口港	zhuǎn kǒu gǎng	Entrepôt , a port where goods are imported, stored, and re-exported without significant processing. Hong Kong's entire colonial economic logic was entrepôt trade, and it retains this function today as a major transshipment hub alongside its role as a financial center.
转世	zhuǎn shì	reincarnation; transmigration; rebirth into a new form — 转 zhuǎn (to turn; to shift; to transmit) + 世 shì (lifetime; generation; world). The specific act of being reborn into a new form, the individual instance of the larger cycle of 轮回.
赚钱	zhuàn qián	To make money, to be profitable — To make money, to be profitable. The opposite pair is 赔钱 (péiqián) or 亏本 (kuīběn). 这个生意不赚钱: this business doesn't make money, the verdict that ends ventures.
篆书	zhuàn shū	seal script
庄子	Zhuāng zǐ	Zhuangzi, the Daoist text and its author
壮美	zhuàng měi	sublime; grand beauty
状语	zhuàng yǔ	adverbial modifier
准备好	zhǔn bèi hǎo	to be ready — Prepare + brought-to-good-state. 准备好了吗? ("ready?") starts every race, road trip, and presentation in the language. The reply 好了 borrows the complement alone, an answer made of pure result.
桌上有书	zhuō shàng yǒu shū	The existential pattern: place + 有 + thing — The canonical existential 有 structure. Place word or place phrase comes first, followed by 有, followed by the indefinite thing being asserted to exist. The place functions as the topic , the frame within which existence is being asserted.
桌子	zhuō zi	table; desk — 桌 zhuō (table) + 子 zi. A textbook example of the bare suffix: the root 桌 rarely stands alone, and 子 makes it a usable noun.
子非鱼，安知鱼之乐？	zǐ fēi yú , ān zhī yú zhī lè ?	You are not a fish — how do you know the happiness of fish? — From 秋水 (Autumn Floods), one of the Outer Chapters. Huizi challenges Zhuangzi's claim that the fish are happy. The exchange is a philosophical demonstration of perspectivism: every claim about the inner states of others is made from outside those states.
子女	zǐn ǚ	sons and daughters; children (collectively) — 子 zǐ (sons) + 女 nǚ (daughters). A formal, collective term for one's children as a group, common in writing about family and law. Here 子 keeps its full third tone.
子午	zǐ wǔ	Midnight and noon branches
紫禁城	Zǐ jìn chéng	Forbidden City
字典	zì diǎn	character dictionary — 字 zì (individual character) + 典 diǎn (canon; standard reference; classic text). A dictionary organized by radical, stroke count, or pronunciation that defines individual characters. The 典 suffix appears in 经典 jīngdiǎn (canonical classics); a 字典 is a canonical reference for individual characters.
字母	zì mǔ	alphabet; letters — 字 zì (character) + 母 mǔ (mother; source; matrix). Literally: "character-mothers," the foundational elements of an alphabetic system from which all words are born. The term applies to any alphabetic system: the English alphabet, the pinyin romanization system, the Cyrillic alphabet.
字幕	zì mù	subtitles; captions — 字 zì (character; text) + 幕 mù (curtain; screen, as in 银幕 yínmù, the silver screen). Literally: "character-curtain." The text that appears across the screen like writing on a curtain. A modern compound that elegantly extends the ancient components into a contemporary context.
字体	zì tǐ	font; typeface; style of writing — 字 zì (character) + 体 tǐ (body; form; style). The physical form a character takes, whether in print, on screen, or in handwriting. Covers both digital fonts and handwriting styles. The same character can appear in multiple 字体: the same 字, different bodies.
字眼	zì yǎn	the key word; the word one fastens on — 字 zì (character; word) + 眼. The eye of the phrase , the single word that carries the weight, that you pivot a sentence on, that an opponent picks at. 抠字眼 kōu zìyǎn "to pick at the wording" (often pejoratively, like English "splitting hairs over phrasing").
自传	zì zhuàn	autobiography — 自 zì (self) + 传 zhuàn (a life record). A biography written by its own subject, the story of a life told in the first person: 写自传 "to write an autobiography." Like 传记, it takes the zhuàn reading.
自从	zì cóng	ever since; from the time that — 自 zì (from) + 从 cóng (from; since). A conjunction marking a starting point in the past, paired with a later clause: 自从他来了以后 "ever since he arrived." Used only of time already begun, never the future.
自大	zì dà	self-aggrandizing; thinking oneself greater than one is; conceited — 自 zì (self) + 大 dà (great; large; important). Consistently negative , the failure of accurate self-assessment in the direction of inflation. Where 骄傲 can sometimes be legitimate pride, 自大 always describes a distortion: the person who claims more importance than they possess.
自动	zì dòng	automatic; automatically; of one's own accord — 自 zì (self) + 动 dòng (to move). Moving by itself, without anyone working it: 自动门 "automatic door," 自动售货机 "vending machine." Also of people acting unprompted: 自动报名 "to sign up on one's own."
自古	zì gǔ	since ancient times
自己	zì jǐ	oneself; myself, yourself, himself (etc.); one's own — 自 zì (self) + 己 jǐ (oneself). The everyday reflexive word, flexing to whatever person the sentence needs: 我自己 "myself," 你自己 "yourself." It also marks possession, 自己的房间 "one's own room," and stresses doing a thing without help.
自己人	zì jǐ rén	one of us; an insider; our own people — 自己 zìjǐ (oneself) + 人 rén. Someone who belongs to your group: your team, your family, your circle of trust. The implied contrast is always 外人 wàirén (outsider). 都是自己人，不用客气 "We're all family here, no need for formality" is an expression of warmth that lowers the social register instantly.
自家	zì jiā	one's own family/people; one's own — 自 zì (self; one's own) + 家 jiā (family; home). Marks something as belonging to or originating from one's own household. Central to the Chinese social concept of insiders vs. outsiders: 自家人 (one of our own) vs. 外人 wàirén (an outsider).
自力	zì lì	self-power (Chan's path)
自满	zì mǎn	complacent; self-satisfied; smug; resting on one's laurels — 自 zì (self) + 满 mǎn (full; satisfied). The state of being full , too full to receive more, too satisfied to keep improving. The classical warning 满招损 is precisely directed at 自满.
自谦	zì qiān	self-deprecating; to understate oneself
自然而然	zì rán ér rán	naturally and inevitably; of its own accord
自然界	zì rán jiè	the natural world; the realm of nature
自然灾害	zì rán zāi hài	natural disaster
自首	zì shǒu	to turn oneself in; to confess to the authorities — 自 zì (oneself) + 首 shǒu (to bow the head, to confess). To give oneself up to the law of one's own accord, before being caught. A legal term: voluntary surrender that often earns a lighter sentence. The head bows itself before justice.
自私	zì sī	selfish
自我	zì wǒ	the self; the ego; self- (in compounds) — 自 zì (self) + 我 wǒ (I; me). The self as an inner concept, the "ego" of psychology and philosophy. As a prefix it forms self-directed actions: 自我介绍 "self-introduction," 自我批评 "self-criticism."
自我介绍	zì wǒ jiè shào	self-introduction
自信	zì xìn	self-confident; confidence in oneself — 自 zì (self) + 信 xìn (to trust; believe). To trust in oneself: 他很自信 "he is very self-assured." A close cousin is 自尊 zìzūn (self-respect), another of the many self- compounds built on 自.
自行车被偷了	zì xíng chē bèi tōu le	the bicycle was stolen — The most prototypical 被 sentence. Theft is unwanted, the subject (bicycle) is the victim, the agent (the thief) may or may not be named. The 了 marks the completion of the unfortunate act.
自由	zì yóu	freedom; liberty; free (to act) — 自 zì (self) + 由 yóu (to follow; from). Literally "following from oneself," to act from one's own will rather than another's: 言论自由 "freedom of speech," 行动自由 "freedom of movement."
自知	zì zhī	self-knowledge
自尊	zì zūn	self-esteem
宗教	zōng jiào	religion — 宗 zōng (ancestor; lineage) + 教 jiào (teaching). The general word for religion, the handed-down teaching that a community is built around: 宗教信仰 "religious belief."
综合	zōng hé	to synthesize; comprehensive; integrated — 综 zōng (to gather; to sum) + 合 hé (to join). To draw many parts into one comprehensive whole: 综合考虑 "to consider comprehensively," 综合大学 "a comprehensive university."
总结	zǒng jié	to sum up; summary
总之	zǒng zhī	"In short" or "all in all — "In short" or "all in all." Conclusion marker that wraps up an explanation. Signals you have said your piece and are now landing the summary: 总之, 我觉得不错 ("all in all, I think it's fine").
粽子	zòng zi	rice dumpling wrapped in leaves — Sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo or reed leaves, traditionally triangular or cylindrical. Made with various fillings: red bean paste, salted egg yolk, cured pork. The characteristic food of the Dragon Boat Festival, eaten to commemorate Qu Yuan.
走遍天下	zǒu biàn tiān xià	to travel the whole world; to have been everywhere — 走遍 zǒu biàn (to walk/travel all over; to cover thoroughly , 遍 is a comprehensive coverage complement) + 天下 (all under heaven; the whole world). The ambition of the traveler: to have seen everything, to have left no corner of the world unvisited.
走出	zǒu chū	to walk out of; to emerge from — 走 zǒu (walk; leave) + 出 (exit complement). The most neutral directional compound: walking across a threshold from inside to outside. Used for physical exits and metaphorical ones , 走出困境 (walk out of a difficult situation), 走出阴影 (emerge from the shadow of something).
走道	zǒu dào	corridor; aisle; walkway — 走 zǒu (walk; go) + 道 (way; path). The path you walk: a corridor between rooms, an aisle on a plane or train, a narrow walkway between structures. Practical and architectural: the space designated for movement through an enclosed or constrained area.
走关系	zǒu guān xi	to use personal connections to get something done — 走 zǒu = to go through; to travel via. 走关系 means to go through the channel of personal connections to accomplish something that might otherwise be difficult or slow.
走后门	zǒu hòu mén	Literally "going through the back door" — Literally "going through the back door": using gifts and personal relationships to obtain favors, preferential treatment, or access that would not be available through formal channels. The phrase acknowledges the reality of this practice without fully endorsing it.
